characters.description: A telepathic waitress at Merlotte's bar in Bon Temps, Louisiana, living alone in her grandmother's house and no longer able to pretend she is outside the supernatural world. She is carrying a killing nobody else knows about, a brother who has been forced into a shape he did not choose, and a growing reputation among vampires and shapeshifters as a human worth using. She is stubborn about doing right by the people she considers hers.
characters.name: Sookie Stackhouse

characters.description: Sookie's brother, a Bon Temps road crew supervisor who was kidnapped and bitten repeatedly by a werepanther the previous winter. Because he was made rather than born, his change is partial and painful: he becomes a hybrid of man and cat rather than a true panther. He faces his first full moon with his sister as his only company, and he is looking for someone to blame.
characters.name: Jason Stackhouse

characters.description: A young woman from the closed werepanther community of Hotshot who is seeing Jason Stackhouse. Her family is not pleased about the connection, and she is caught between them and him.
characters.name: Crystal Norris

characters.description: Sookie's boss, the owner of Merlotte's and a shapeshifter. He is shot in the leg outside his own bar early in the book, which puts him on crutches and leaves Sookie effectively running the place.
characters.name: Sam Merlotte

characters.description: A short-order cook newly hired at Merlotte's. She has worked kitchens in small towns all over the region, never staying long anywhere, and she is friendly enough without being anybody's friend.
characters.name: Sweetie Des Arts

characters.description: Sookie's friend from school, who runs a dress shop in Bon Temps. Her arrangement with a wealthy Mississippi vampire has been handed on to someone else without her consent, and she is frightened, bruised and unwilling to explain.
characters.name: Tara Thornton

characters.description: Sookie's former lover, the vampire who lives across the cemetery from her, returned from his travels in South America. He wants her back and she does not want him, and their dealings are civil, frequent and uncomfortable.
characters.name: Bill Compton

characters.description: The head of the Hotshot werepanther community and a road crew foreman, a steady, courteous man who has made no secret of wanting to marry Sookie. He is among those shot by the sniper working the area.
characters.name: Calvin Norris

characters.description: The thousand-year-old vampire sheriff of the area, restored to himself after the witches' curse and, as far as anyone can tell, with no memory of the weeks he spent hidden in Sookie's house. He lends Merlotte's a bartender while Sam is laid up, and he keeps finding reasons to have Sookie where he can see her.
characters.name: Eric Northman

characters.description: A small, red-haired English vampire lent to Merlotte's by Eric to tend bar while Sam recovers. Elaborately courteous, he wears an eyepatch, tells stories of a piratical life at sea, and is popular with the customers.
characters.name: Charles Twining

characters.description: The leader of the Shreveport werewolf pack, a retired air force officer who has run pack business with military discipline. His death leaves the packmaster's place open at the worst possible time.
characters.name: Colonel Flood

characters.description: The Shreveport werewolf who has twice been Sookie's ally, now backing his father's claim to lead the pack. He asks Sookie to serve as an impartial witness at the contest, which puts her in the middle of pack politics she has no standing in.
characters.name: Alcide Herveaux

characters.description: Alcide's father, who runs the family surveying company and considers himself the natural successor as packmaster. Proud, aging and heavily in debt from gambling, he is not as strong a candidate as his son believes.
characters.name: Jackson Herveaux

characters.description: A Shreveport motorcycle dealer and werewolf, the other candidate for packmaster. Ordinary-looking and widely liked among the pack's rank and file, he wants the position badly.
characters.name: Patrick Furnan

characters.description: A vampire who has taken over Tara Thornton's arrangement from her previous protector. He is small, cruel and territorial, he answers to a powerful vampire elsewhere, and he treats Tara as property to be damaged as he likes.
characters.name: Mickey

characters.description: A private investigator hired, with his wife Lily, by the Pelt family of Jackson to find out what became of their daughter Debbie. He is thorough, polite and hard to lie to, and he does not believe Sookie's account of the last time she saw her.
characters.name: Jack Leeds

characters.description: The tall, beautiful woman who appeared at Sookie's side during the fight with the witches and would not say what she was. She continues to turn up when Sookie is in danger, cheerfully unhelpful about her own nature, and admits only that looking after Sookie is a duty of hers.
characters.name: Claudine

recaps.ending: Both threats turn out to have been sitting inside Merlotte's all along. The sniper is Sweetie Des Arts, the short-order cook, who was bitten by a shapeshifter years ago, became something she despises, and has been moving from town to town killing two-natured people ever since. She corners Sookie with a rifle and is killed before she can fire, and the shootings stop. Sam, Calvin Norris and the others she wounded recover. The second threat is Charles Twining, the courteous English vampire Eric lent to the bar. He set the fire at Sookie's house and he attacks her openly at the end: he was sent to Louisiana to avenge Long Shadow, the vampire Eric destroyed at Fangtasia years earlier, and killing Eric's favorite human was the closest he could get. He is destroyed. The werewolf pack ends the book under Patrick Furnan, who cheated his way through the contest; Jackson Herveaux is dead, and Alcide, who blames Sookie for not preventing it, is no longer easy company. Tara Thornton is free of Mickey, bought out of the arrangement by Eric at a price Sookie will owe. Bill is back in Bon Temps and unwelcome. The last word belongs to Eric, who tells Sookie that his memory has come back: he remembers the weeks in her house, their nights together, and Debbie Pelt dying on her kitchen floor, which means Sookie's one real secret is now shared with the most dangerous person she knows.
recaps.in_short: Sookie sees her brother Jason through his first full moon as a bitten werepanther, then finds that someone is shooting shapeshifters across the parish: Sam Merlotte is hit in the leg, Calvin Norris is wounded, and a young woman is killed. Running the bar in Sam's place, Sookie takes on a vampire bartender lent by Eric, an Englishman named Charles Twining. Her house is set on fire in the night and she barely escapes. Meanwhile the Shreveport werewolf pack loses its leader and holds a contest to replace him; Sookie is asked to witness, sees Patrick Furnan cheat, and cannot stop the contest that kills Alcide's father. Private investigators hired by Debbie Pelt's family press her about the disappearance she is responsible for, and she has to get Eric's help to free her friend Tara from a brutal vampire. Sookie works out that the sniper is Sweetie Des Arts, the bar's own cook, a woman bitten years ago who hates what she became; Sweetie is killed. Charles then attacks Sookie, revealed as an assassin avenging a vampire Eric destroyed, and is destroyed himself. Eric ends the book by telling Sookie that he remembers everything.

recaps.text: Sookie Stackhouse is a telepathic waitress at Merlotte's bar in Bon Temps, Louisiana, in a world where vampires live openly. Her grandmother was murdered by a man hunting Sookie; her boss Sam Merlotte is a shapeshifter; and she has survived a maenad, the anti-vampire Fellowship of the Sun, and a vampire kingdom's politics. Her relationship with the vampire Bill Compton ended after he planned to leave her for his maker and then, starving and out of his mind, nearly killed her during his own rescue in Mississippi; she killed his maker herself. She is watched, wanted and repeatedly used by Eric Northman, the thousand-year-old sheriff of the area. Last winter a coven cursed Eric with amnesia, Sookie hid him in her house for pay, and they became lovers; when the curse broke he remembered none of it. On the same night, Debbie Pelt broke in to kill Sookie and Sookie shot her dead, a killing Eric helped conceal and then forgot, leaving Sookie the only person who knows. Her brother Jason was kidnapped and bitten by a werepanther from the isolated community of Hotshot and will now change with the full moon. Sookie is also guarded, on and off, by a beautiful woman named Claudine who will not explain what she is.

Sookie spends the first full moon of Jason's new life with him, out at his house by the pond, because there is no one else to do it. Because he was bitten rather than born to it, his change is partial and agonizing and leaves him a hybrid of man and cat, an object of contempt to the born werepanthers of Hotshot. He is furious about it and looking for someone to punish. Back in town, Sam Merlotte is shot in the leg by a rifle as he steps out of Merlotte's, and the bar is left without an owner on his feet. Sookie takes on the running of it, hires help, and starts hearing about other shootings in the area. The victims have nothing obvious in common until Sookie sees what the police cannot: every one of them is two-natured.

The shootings continue. Calvin Norris, the head of Hotshot, is badly wounded, and a young woman is killed outright, and the shapeshifter community of the parish realizes it is being hunted by someone who knows what they are. Sookie, who now has to keep Merlotte's staffed at night, accepts Eric Northman's offer of a bartender: Charles Twining, a small, courteous English vampire with an eyepatch and a stock of stories about a life at sea, who proves to be very good with customers. Bill Compton comes home from South America and starts finding reasons to be near Sookie, who does not want him back. The Shreveport werewolf pack loses Colonel Flood, its longtime leader, and the pack's succession is suddenly an open question.

Alcide Herveaux asks Sookie to serve as an impartial witness at the contest that will decide the next packmaster, between his father Jackson Herveaux and Patrick Furnan, a motorcycle dealer with the rank and file behind him. Sookie also has her friend Tara Thornton to worry about: Tara's arrangement with a wealthy vampire has been handed on to Mickey, a vicious vampire who is hurting her and whom Tara is too frightened to leave. Sookie asks Eric for help, which costs her. On top of that, private investigators hired by Debbie Pelt's family arrive from Jackson, asking careful questions about the night Debbie disappeared, and Sookie, who shot her, has to lie to their faces without any assurance that they believe her.

Sookie's house is set on fire in the night. She gets out alive, but part of the house is gutted, most of what her grandmother left her is ruined, and a man's body is found in the burned area. She is left camping in what remains and depending on the goodwill of people she does not entirely trust, with money from the pack and the vampires paying for the repairs. Eric handles Mickey, and Tara is freed from him at a price that will be Sookie's to pay eventually. Between the sniper, the arson, the pack's succession fight and the Pelts' investigators, Sookie cannot tell which of the several people circling her is the one actually trying to kill her.

The packmaster contest is held, and Sookie, witnessing, sees Patrick Furnan cheat in one of the trials. She cannot stop what follows: the contest ends in a fight to the death, and Jackson Herveaux is killed. Furnan becomes packmaster of Shreveport. Alcide, grieving and looking for a reason, blames Sookie for not preventing it, and the friendship between them goes cold. Sookie, meanwhile, works out the pattern behind the shootings by thinking about who has been present in every town where a shapeshifter was shot, rather than about who hates them.

The sniper is Sweetie Des Arts, the short-order cook at Merlotte's, who was bitten by a shapeshifter years ago, became a thing she cannot stand being, and has since moved from town to town killing two-natured people. She corners Sookie with the rifle and is killed before she can use it, and the shootings end. That same night Charles Twining attacks Sookie in the open. The polite English bartender was sent to Louisiana to avenge Long Shadow, the vampire Eric destroyed at Fangtasia years ago; he set the fire at Sookie's house, and killing Eric's favorite human was the nearest thing to revenge available to him. He is destroyed. Sam recovers, Tara is free of Mickey, and Sookie is left with a half-burned house and a ruined friendship with Alcide. Then Eric comes to tell her that his memory has returned: he remembers the weeks in her house, what they were to each other, and Debbie Pelt dying on her kitchen floor.

characters.description: Chicago's professional wizard, now sharing his tiny basement apartment with his half-brother Thomas and a rapidly growing dog. With Murphy out of town, Harry is blackmailed into a hunt for a dead necromancer's lost book while the necromancer's surviving disciples descend on Chicago for Halloween, each meaning to use what the book unlocks to seize godlike power. Maimed hand, mounting debts to dark powers, and a war still on his shoulders - and still nobody better positioned to stand in the way.
characters.name: Harry Dresden

characters.description: Harry's half-brother, the White Court vampire, now sleeping on Harry's couch after being cut off by his family. Thomas is struggling - trying to hold down mortal jobs, trying not to feed, and chafing against everything his nature demands - and the friction of two proud, private men sharing one small apartment runs through the book. When the fighting starts, he is exactly the ally a wizard wants at his back.
characters.name: Thomas Raith

characters.description: The ancient Black Court vampire, neither dead nor done with Harry. Mavra opens the book with blackmail: she holds evidence that could destroy Karrin Murphy's career and freedom, and she will use it unless Harry finds her a legendary necromancer's lost text, The Word of Kemmler, within three days. Cold, patient, and untroubled by the apocalyptic potential of what she is asking for, she sets the whole plot in motion.
characters.name: Mavra

characters.description: A slight, wiry, polka-loving medical examiner - the one who was institutionalized for reporting the truth about corpses that were not human. Waldo Butters is no fighter and makes no pretense of courage, which is exactly what makes his courage matter: dragged into the necromancers' war over the bodies in his morgue, he stays, helps, and grows. His medical skill, his curiosity, and his one-man polka band all turn out to be surprisingly load-bearing.
characters.name: Waldo Butters

characters.description: The spirit of intellect in the skull in Harry's lab - and, this case reveals, a store of darker history than Harry knew. Bob's knowledge of necromancy is firsthand: the skull once served Heinrich Kemmler himself, the necromancer whose disciples are converging on Chicago, and there is a part of Bob's own past that Harry must handle with extreme care. His lore on the Erlking and on Kemmler's methods becomes the key to everything.
characters.name: Bob

characters.description: Harry's dog, no longer a puppy: a huge, gray, preternaturally intelligent Foo dog whose senses for the uncanny outstrip any ward. Mouse is calm, deliberate, and devoted, and in this book he proves he is not merely large but genuinely supernatural - an ally in his own right when the dead start walking.
characters.name: Mouse

characters.description: The most straightforwardly brutal of Kemmler's surviving disciples: a tall, cadaverous necromancer who walks Chicago with an entourage of zombies and a habit of raising the freshly dead as enforcers. Grevane wants the Word of Kemmler and the power it unlocks, and he interrogates, kills, and animates his way toward it. Of the rivals converging on the city, he is the bluntest instrument - which does not make him the least dangerous.
characters.name: Grevane

characters.description: A necromancer in a concealing hood and cloak whose power dwarfs the other disciples - in a direct clash, more than a match for Harry. Cowl speaks with dry courtesy, works with a similarly hooded partner called Kumori, and his true identity stays hidden behind the cowl he is named for. Of everyone hunting Kemmler's legacy, he is the one whose plans reach furthest, and the one Harry has the least idea how to stop.
characters.name: Cowl

characters.description: A disciple of Kemmler whose specialty is the theft of bodies: the Corpsetaker trades minds with victims, wearing stolen flesh and discarding it, so that no face can be trusted twice. Ancient, cunning, and patient, the Corpsetaker hunts the Word of Kemmler alongside the other disciples, and the body-swapping makes every encounter a potential ambush from inside someone Harry trusts.
characters.name: The Corpsetaker

characters.description: The shadow of the fallen angel whose coin Harry buried under his lab - present in his mind since the day he touched it, and in this book, no longer silent. The shadow can shape what Harry perceives, offers him knowledge and power with perfect helpfulness, and wants exactly what every Denarian's coin wants: for Harry to take up the real thing. Its unmasking forces Harry to reckon with what he has been carrying for the past year.
characters.name: Lasciel's shadow

characters.description: Captain of the Wardens of the White Council, the wizards' soldiers and enforcers. Luccio arrives in Chicago with a battered handful of Wardens - the corps has been gutted by the vampire war - to face the necromancer crisis. A career soldier of centuries' standing, forthright and fair, she weighs Harry by what he does rather than by his file, and what happens to her in Chicago changes her life permanently.
characters.name: Anastasia Luccio

recaps.ending: The Darkhallow fails. On Halloween night, with the city's dead walking, Harry disrupts the ritual that would have made one of Kemmler's disciples a god: the vast well of spiritual power is never claimed, and the storm of necromancy breaks. Grevane and the Corpsetaker fall out and fight among themselves; Grevane dies in the chaos, and Harry personally shoots the Corpsetaker after realizing the mind-swapping necromancer had stolen the body of Warden-Captain Luccio - leaving Luccio alive but permanently housed in the young body the Corpsetaker had been wearing. Cowl is buried in the collapse of his own ritual, no corpse ever confirmed. Harry's improbable cavalry is the book's signature image: using Kemmler's own methods, he animates Sue, the museum's Tyrannosaurus skeleton, and rides her into the battle with Butters drumming the polka beat that sustains the spell. The fallen Denarian Cassius dies in an earlier ambush, spitting a death curse at Harry: die alone. In the aftermath, the decimated White Council drafts Harry into the Wardens as regional commander for the central United States - the wizard cops who once watched him for a chance to execute him now issue him a gray cloak - and Luccio's own sword-forging talent is lost with her old body. Mavra's blackmail hold over Murphy is broken, Butters has found his courage, and Harry has admitted at last that the shadow of Lasciel lives in his head - an enemy inside the walls, still there as the book closes.
recaps.in_short: With Murphy away, the vampire Mavra blackmails Harry - evidence that would destroy Murphy's career against the recovery of The Word of Kemmler, the lost book of history's worst necromancer. Kemmler's surviving disciples - zombie-raising Grevane, the body-stealing Corpsetaker, and the hooded, hugely powerful Cowl - converge on Chicago to use the book for the Darkhallow, a Halloween ritual to devour the city's dead and ascend to godhood. Aided by his brother Thomas, the skull-spirit Bob (who once served Kemmler himself), his Foo dog Mouse, and the timid, polka-loving medical examiner Waldo Butters, Harry fights zombie hordes, survives the Denarian Cassius's ambush and death curse, summons the Erlking's wild hunt into his enemies' path, and finally admits the shadow of the fallen angel Lasciel has been living in his mind since Death Masks. On Halloween night he animates Sue, the museum's T. rex skeleton, rides her into battle, and breaks the Darkhallow: Grevane dies, Harry kills the Corpsetaker - who had body-swapped with Warden-Captain Luccio, leaving her in a young stranger's body - and Cowl vanishes in the collapse. The gutted White Council drafts Harry into the Wardens, and Murphy is safe.

recaps.text: Previously: Harry Dresden learned that Thomas Raith, the White Court vampire who kept saving his life, is his half-brother - both sons of Margaret LeFay, whom the White King, Lord Raith, murdered. Harry and Thomas survived Raith's trap; their mother's death curse had secretly left the king powerless, and Lara Raith now rules the White Court behind her father's figurehead throne. Thomas, cut off from his family, moved into Harry's apartment. The costs are mounting: Harry's left hand was burned nearly useless in a daylight raid on the Black Court vampire Mavra's nest - a raid made with Murphy and the mercenary Kincaid - and he learned his old mentor Ebenezar McCoy is the Blackstaff, the Council's secret assassin. Harry still hides the shadow of the fallen angel Lasciel, taken into his mind when he grabbed her coin to save a child; the coin lies buried under his lab. The wizards' war with the Red Court grinds on, and the Wardens are being bled dry.

With Murphy on holiday with Kincaid, Mavra of the Black Court comes to collect her grudge in a new currency: blackmail. She holds evidence that would send Murphy to prison, and her price is The Word of Kemmler - the lost final text of Heinrich Kemmler, the necromancer so terrible the White Council killed him seven times - delivered within three days. Harry starts hunting the book and immediately trips over the competition: Grevane, a disciple of Kemmler, is in Chicago with an entourage of zombies, tearing through anyone connected to the text. At the morgue, medical examiner Waldo Butters shows Harry bodies that mark the killers' trail, and promptly gets dragged along when the trail doubles back onto them. Bob the skull, it emerges, knows Kemmler's work uncomfortably well.

The field grows crowded: besides Grevane there is the Corpsetaker, an ancient horror who swaps minds with victims and wears their stolen bodies, and Cowl, a hooded necromancer whose raw power exceeds anything Harry can match head-on - each disciple hunting the Word, each planning to use it on Halloween night for the Darkhallow, a ritual that would devour the spirits of the city's dead and elevate its caster to godhood. Harry learns Bob's buried history - the skull once served Kemmler himself - and recovers a darker sub-personality of the spirit with great care. Attacks and reprisals escalate: zombies against wards, ghouls in the streets, and Harry, Thomas, Butters and Mouse increasingly under siege. The numbers say Harry cannot beat even one disciple in open battle, let alone three.

Harry works the angles instead of the head-on fight. Deciphering Kemmler's methods with Bob, he identifies what the Darkhallow needs - and what might wreck it. An old enemy resurfaces: Cassius, the ex-Denarian stripped of his coin in the Shroud affair, ambushes and tortures Harry; the fight ends with Cassius dying at bay - Butters and Mouse proving braver than either believed - and spending his last breath on a sorcerer's death curse: die alone. Battered, Harry makes a dangerous play for position: using the disciples' own lore, he arranges to summon the Erlking, the lord of the wild hunt whose presence on Halloween the necromancers themselves mean to exploit, and to drop the hunt into his enemies' path rather than let them harness it.

The pieces converge on Halloween night. The summoning gambit half-works and half-explodes: the Erlking's wild hunt is loosed into the necromancers' game, the disciples turn on one another as the Darkhallow's hour approaches, and the city's dead begin to rise across Chicago. In the chaos Harry finally names the thing he has been refusing to see: the too-helpful presence shaping his perceptions - including a woman he believed real - is the shadow of Lasciel, alive in his mind since the day he grabbed her coin, patiently angling for him to dig the real thing up. Knowing his enemy within, Harry accepts the shadow's knowledge on his own terms and commits to the maddest plan of his career: if the ritual needs ancient dead power, he will bring older and bigger dead than anyone - starting at the Field Museum, where a Tyrannosaurus skeleton named Sue is about to get a new job. The Wardens, led by Captain Luccio, arrive in the city, bloodied by the war but ready to fight.

Riding the animated skeleton of Sue the T. rex - with Butters pounding the polka rhythm that binds the spell - Harry smashes into the Darkhallow. The ritual collapses without an ascendant: Grevane and the Corpsetaker turn on each other and Grevane dies; Cowl is buried in the implosion of his own working, his death never confirmed. Harry discovers the Corpsetaker's final theft - the necromancer had swapped bodies with Captain Luccio - and shoots the impostor wearing Luccio's old flesh, leaving the real Luccio permanently housed in the young body the Corpsetaker had worn. With the crisis broken, Mavra's hold over Murphy is finished. The gutted White Council, seven Wardens dead for every one recruited, does the unthinkable: it drafts Harry Dresden into the Wardens as regional commander for the central United States. Harry ends the book in a gray cloak he never wanted, with a brother on his couch, a polka-powered friend for life, and a fallen angel's shadow still waiting in his head.

characters.description: A telepathic waitress and now part owner of Merlotte's, living alone in her grandmother's house with her fairy relatives gone and her one wish spent. Her marriage to Eric Northman is finished in everything but name, she is out of favor with the vampires who used to protect her, and the ordinary business of running a bar in Bon Temps is most of what she has left.
characters.name: Sookie Stackhouse

characters.description: The shapeshifter who owns Merlotte's, Sookie's business partner and closest friend, recently returned from the dead and not comfortable in his own life since. He is grateful, unsettled and awkward with her in ways neither of them can name.
characters.name: Sam Merlotte

characters.description: The Viking vampire sheriff of Area Five, still bound by the marriage contract his dead maker signed on his behalf with the queen of Oklahoma. He and Sookie are barely speaking; she chose to spend her one wish on someone else, and he has not pretended it did not matter.
characters.name: Eric Northman

characters.description: Sookie's vampire neighbor, steady and undemanding, who has stopped competing for her and simply keeps himself available. He is one of the few people whose loyalty to her has never been conditional on anything.
characters.name: Bill Compton

characters.description: Eric's child and lieutenant, running Fangtasia and openly contemptuous of the Oklahoma arrangement. She would rather see her maker fight it than accept it, and she has little patience left for Sookie's part in the situation.
characters.name: Pam Ravenscroft

characters.description: Sookie's brother, settled at last and engaged to Michele Schubert. He has become genuinely reliable, which is new, and he stands by his sister without needing to be asked.
characters.name: Jason Stackhouse

characters.description: Sookie's former friend and fellow waitress at Merlotte's, released from prison after her part in a plot against Sookie's life. Broke, unemployable and full of grievance, she comes to the bar to ask for her old job back.
characters.name: Arlene Fowler

characters.description: A half-demon lawyer who has handled supernatural estates around New Orleans for many years and who was a friend of Sookie's fairy grandfather Fintan. Precise, courteous and enormously well connected, he arrives with information about Sookie's family that nobody else has ever offered her.
characters.name: Desmond Cataliades

characters.description: Mr. Cataliades's niece, a part-demon young woman who dresses in whatever colors come to hand, speaks in a rapid run-on, and is a great deal more dangerous than she looks. She works as her uncle's messenger and muscle.
characters.name: Diantha

characters.description: The vampire queen of Oklahoma, who holds a marriage contract signed by Eric's maker before his death. Handsome, direct and used to getting her way, she comes to Louisiana to see what she has bought.
characters.name: Freyda

characters.description: A wealthy New Orleans developer, father of Sookie's friend Amelia, who spent months trying to get hold of the fairy token Sookie's grandmother left her. Losing it has not made him lose interest in her.
characters.name: Copley Carmichael

characters.description: The former head of the anti-vampire Fellowship of the Sun, disgraced and stripped of his church, now a diminished figure living on other people's tolerance. His hatred of Sookie has survived everything else about him.
characters.name: Steve Newlin

characters.description: Eric's day man, a werewolf who guards his privacy fiercely and does his job exactly. He keeps his distance from Sookie's affairs and from everyone else's, and volunteers nothing about his own.
characters.name: Mustapha Khan

characters.description: A vampire made by Eric long before Pam, cool and self-contained, who has been keeping watch over Sookie on her maker's orders without ever introducing herself.
characters.name: Karin

recaps.ending: The murder case against Sookie falls apart, the group of old enemies working against her is broken up, and the danger to her is ended rather than merely postponed. Her friends and the vampires who still owe her, including Bill, Pam and Karin, are what carry her through it. Mr. Cataliades leaves her with the answer to a question she has had all her life: her telepathy is a gift he made long ago to the descendants of his friend Fintan who were born with the spark to hold it, which is why she has it and Jason does not. Eric's marriage contract with Freyda cannot be broken, and he goes to Oklahoma. He and Sookie part deliberately and finally, each understanding that the other made a choice they could not undo, and the vampire marriage between them is over. Sookie keeps her half of Merlotte's, keeps her house, and stops trying to live in the supernatural world's politics. Sam, alive because of what she spent, is the person she chooses and who chooses her, and the series closes with the two of them together and Sookie's life her own for the first time since the night a vampire first walked into the bar.
recaps.in_short: Sookie's one wish is spent, her fairy relatives are gone, and her marriage to Eric is finished in all but name while the queen of Oklahoma presses the contract that will take him away. Then Arlene Fowler, just out of prison for conspiring to kill her, turns up at Merlotte's asking for her job back and is found strangled behind the bar days later, and Sookie is arrested for the murder. The case against her is part of something arranged: a group of people who hate her, backed by money and by a bargain-maker willing to trade in favors, have set out to destroy her by law first and by force afterward. Her friends, her brother, and the vampires who still stand by her hold the line while the frame comes apart. Mr. Cataliades, a half-demon lawyer, reveals that Sookie's telepathy was his gift to her fairy grandfather's line. In the end Sookie is cleared, Eric leaves for Oklahoma for good, and Sookie makes a life with Sam.

recaps.text: Sookie Stackhouse is a telepathic waitress and part owner of Merlotte's in Bon Temps, Louisiana, where vampires and shapeshifters live openly. She is part fairy through her great-grandfather Prince Niall Brigant, who closed Faery permanently after a war fought over his human-blooded descendants nearly killed her. Her grandmother left her a cluviel dor, a fairy token good for one wish, and Sookie spent it bringing her employer Sam Merlotte back from the dead during the fight that exposed the werewolf Jannalynn Hopper as the architect of a murder meant to disgrace Eric Northman. Eric, the vampire sheriff Sookie married by vampire custom, understood that she could have used the wish to release him from the marriage contract his dead maker signed with Freyda, queen of Oklahoma, and their relationship has not survived it. Niall has taken Sookie's cousin Claude away for treachery and her great-uncle Dermot has gone home to Faery. Louisiana still belongs to Felipe de Castro, who has never learned who killed his regent.

Sookie is living alone and working, with the fairies gone from her house and the cluviel dor used up. Sam is alive and grateful and strange with her; having died and come back has left him unsure of himself, and neither of them is willing to talk plainly about what she spent to do it. Eric will not see her, Pam is barely civil, and the marriage everyone in the vampire world knows about is over in every way except paperwork. Into this comes Arlene Fowler, released from prison after her part in a plot to have Sookie killed, wanting her old waitressing job back as though nothing had happened. Sookie refuses her. Arlene leaves the bar angry and makes sure several people hear about it.

Arlene is found dead behind Merlotte's, strangled and left in the dumpster, and the parish arrests Sookie for her murder. The evidence is circumstantial but tidy, the public quarrel is remembered by half the bar, and Bon Temps divides sharply over whether the telepathic woman who consorts with vampires is capable of it. Sookie spends time in a cell before she is bailed out, and comes home to find her name in the papers and her business damaged. Meanwhile the queen of Oklahoma sends word that she intends to enforce the marriage contract on Eric, and the vampires of Area Five begin to arrange themselves around a departure nobody wants to name.

It becomes clear that Sookie has not simply been unlucky. A number of people with old grievances against her have been brought together and financed, among them Copley Carmichael, who never got the fairy token he wanted, and Steve Newlin, whose ruined church left him nothing but his hatred; behind the arrangement is something that deals in favors rather than money. The plan is to destroy Sookie by law and, if that fails, more directly. Her defense is her friends: Jason and Michele, Bill, Sam and the lawyers Sam can afford. Desmond Cataliades, a half-demon attorney who was a friend of her fairy grandfather Fintan, arrives with his niece Diantha and tells Sookie where her telepathy actually came from, along with a warning about what is being organized against her.

The pressure moves from the courthouse to Sookie's doorstep. Eric's day man Mustapha Khan disappears, and it emerges that he has been leaned on through someone he cares about rather than turning of his own accord. Attempts are made on Sookie directly, and she discovers she has had a guard she never knew about: Karin, an older child of Eric's, set to watch her house. The murder case begins to come apart as the people who assembled it fall out with one another, and Sookie's friends work backwards from the conspirators to the death itself. Freyda arrives in person to collect what the contract owes her, and Eric, who cannot break an agreement made by his maker, prepares to leave Louisiana.

The frame collapses and the conspiracy against Sookie is broken, its members dead, ruined or scattered, and the charges against her dropped. Mr. Cataliades explains the last of her family's history: the telepathy is a gift he made long ago to Fintan's descendants who were born able to carry it, which is why it fell on Sookie and Hunter and not on Jason. Eric's contract stands. He and Sookie say goodbye deliberately rather than bitterly, and he goes to Oklahoma as Freyda's husband, ending the vampire marriage and, with it, Sookie's place in vampire politics. She keeps her house, her half of Merlotte's, and the friends who stood up for her when the parish believed she was a murderer. Sam, alive because of the wish she spent on him, finally says what he has not been able to say since he came back, and Sookie chooses him. The series ends with her ordinary life restored to her and shared.

characters.description: A telepathic waitress in Bon Temps, recovering slowly from the torture she survived at the hands of two fairies. She is physically scarred, sleeping badly, and flinching at things that never bothered her before. She is married to Eric Northman by vampire custom, cut off from Faery since her great-grandfather closed it, and sharing her house with fairy relatives she is still learning to live with.
characters.name: Sookie Stackhouse

characters.description: The Viking vampire sheriff of Area Five, owner of Fangtasia, and Sookie's husband by vampire law. He is under constant pressure from Victor Madden, the regent Nevada placed over him, and he is more careful with Sookie than he has ever been while telling her less than she wants to know about his own past.
characters.name: Eric Northman

characters.description: Eric's child and second in command at Fangtasia, blunt, sardonic and completely loyal to her maker. She treats Sookie with a wary respect that has grown into something close to friendship.
characters.name: Pam Ravenscroft

characters.description: Sookie's vampire neighbor, still weak and badly damaged by the fairy blood that poisoned him when he saved her. His recovery has stalled, he refuses to explain why, and Sookie's anger at his original deception has softened into worry.
characters.name: Bill Compton

characters.description: The shapeshifter who owns Merlotte's, now publicly known as two-natured along with the rest of his kind. Business at the bar has suffered since the revelation, and he is dating Jannalynn Hopper of the Shreveport werewolf pack.
characters.name: Sam Merlotte

characters.description: Sookie's brother, widowed by Crystal's murder and steadier than he has been in years. He has started seeing Michele Schubert, a woman with no patience for nonsense, and is trying to be a better neighbor to his sister than he used to be.
characters.name: Jason Stackhouse

characters.description: Claudine's brother, a beautiful and vain part-fairy stranded on the human side when Faery closed. Cut off from his own world and grieving his sister, he attaches himself to Sookie as the only close kin he has left and moves into her house.
characters.name: Claude Crane

characters.description: Sookie's great-uncle, a fairy who could pass for Jason's twin, likewise stranded outside Faery. Something has been done to his mind that leaves him unreliable and easily led, and he drifts in and out of Sookie's house doing odd jobs while nobody can quite decide whether to trust him.
characters.name: Dermot Brigant

characters.description: The Roman vampire who made Eric more than a thousand years ago and who still holds the authority of a maker over him. Courteous, ancient and utterly certain of his rights, he arrives in Louisiana unannounced and expects Eric to accommodate him and his companion.
characters.name: Appius Livius Ocella

characters.description: Appius's other surviving child, a vampire in the body of a boy of about thirteen, turned out of the wreckage of the Russian imperial family. He is charming in short bursts, physically strong beyond his size, and visibly unwell in his mind, and the household around him grows tense whenever he is quiet.
characters.name: Alexei Romanov

characters.description: Packmaster of the Long Tooth werewolves in Shreveport, an old friend of Sookie's who keeps finding reasons to visit her land. He wants her formally tied to his pack and is not always honest about how he goes about it.
characters.name: Alcide Herveaux

characters.description: The Long Tooth pack's enforcer, a small, sharply dressed young werewolf with an appetite for violence that her size disguises. She is dating Sam, which everyone regards as an unlikely pairing, and she carries out Alcide's discipline without hesitation.
characters.name: Jannalynn Hopper

characters.description: Alcide's second in command, a capable and well-liked werewolf brought in from outside the parish. He has a keen nose and is the one who reports that something is buried in the woods on Sookie's property.
characters.name: Basim al Saud

characters.description: Sookie's cousin Hadley's small son, living in Red Ditch with his father Remy. He is telepathic like Sookie, about to start school, and has no idea yet that the thoughts he hears are not something other children can hear too.
characters.name: Hunter Savoy

characters.description: A fairy stranded on the human side, who was Claudine's lover and the father of the child she was carrying when she died. He holds Sookie responsible for that death and has come looking for a reckoning.
characters.name: Colman

recaps.ending: The visit from Eric's maker ends in the woods behind Sookie's house. Alexei, past any control, has already killed Eric's day man Bobby Burnham and the vampire Felicia, and the final fight destroys both him and Appius Livius Ocella, who dies of the wounds his own child gave him. Colman, the fairy who came to avenge Claudine, dies in the same night's violence, ending that debt. Sookie is hurt again but alive, and Eric is left grieving a maker he both loved and could never refuse, with the ties to his own past finally cut. The body buried on Sookie's land is identified as Alcide's second, Basim al Saud, killed by the Long Tooth pack after he was found to be working against Alcide; the pack settles the matter internally and Sookie's land is cleared. Bill's poisoning is finally healed and he begins to recover his strength. Claude and Dermot remain in Sookie's house, Dermot still under whatever was done to his mind, and Sookie has found a place for herself as the person teaching Hunter how to live with telepathy. Victor Madden's rivalry with Eric is unresolved and getting worse.
recaps.in_short: Sookie is recovering badly from her torture when Eric's maker, the Roman vampire Appius Livius Ocella, arrives uninvited with his other child, Alexei Romanov, a boy vampire out of the murdered Russian imperial family whose mind never survived what was done to him. Alexei's presence destabilizes everything: he escapes control, kills Eric's day man and one of his vampires, and forces a hunt through the woods behind Sookie's house that ends with both Alexei and Appius destroyed. Alongside this, a body is found buried on Sookie's land and proves to be Alcide's second, Basim al Saud, killed by his own pack for conspiring against the packmaster, and a grieving fairy named Colman comes to make Sookie pay for Claudine's death and dies in the same night's fighting. Sookie's cousins Claude and Dermot settle into her house, Bill slowly heals, and Sookie begins teaching Hunter to manage his telepathy before he starts school.

recaps.text: Sookie Stackhouse is a telepathic waitress in Bon Temps, Louisiana, where vampires live openly and the world's shapeshifters and werewolves have now revealed themselves too. Louisiana belongs to Felipe de Castro of Nevada, who conquered it after a bombing and a hurricane left the old queen helpless, and his regent Victor Madden sits over Eric Northman, the vampire sheriff Sookie is married to by vampire custom. Sookie is part fairy through her great-grandfather Prince Niall Brigant. A fairy war fought over Niall's human-blooded descendants nearly killed her: she was abducted and tortured by two of the enemy's servants, her fairy godmother Claudine and her bodyguard Tray Dawson were killed, and Bill Compton was poisoned saving her. Niall ended the war and then closed Faery permanently, stranding part-fairies such as Claude and Dermot on the human side. Sookie's brother Jason is a widower after his wife Crystal's murder, and Sookie has a small telepathic cousin, Hunter, whom she is quietly helping.

Sookie is healing far more slowly than she admits. The scars are visible and the fear is not: she jumps at noises, avoids the woods, and cannot make herself feel safe in her own house. Claude, grieving his sister and locked out of Faery, invites himself to live with her, and Dermot begins turning up as well, working on the house and behaving as though his thoughts are not entirely his own. Bill remains weak from the fairy poisoning and will not explain why he is not recovering. Then Eric tells Sookie that his maker is coming: Appius Livius Ocella, who turned him more than a thousand years ago and whose authority over him has never lapsed. Appius arrives with a companion, a vampire in the body of a boy, and installs himself in Eric's life without being asked.

The boy is Alexei Romanov, Appius's other child, taken out of the massacre of the Russian imperial family and never made whole afterward. He is charming when he chooses and frightening when he does not, and Appius manages him the way one manages a fire. Eric, reduced by his maker's presence to something less than the sheriff he is, cannot refuse either of them. Elsewhere, Alcide asks to use Sookie's woods for the pack's runs, and his second, Basim al Saud, reports that a body has been buried on her property and that fairies have been on the land. Sookie also spends a day with Hunter, teaching him what to do with the thoughts he cannot help hearing before he starts school and gives himself away.

Alexei's condition worsens. He slips his keepers, and Appius's confidence that he can be contained looks increasingly like denial. At the same time Sookie learns she is being hunted on her own account: Colman, a fairy who was Claudine's lover and the father of her unborn child, blames Sookie for Claudine's death and has been circling the property. The buried body on her land is dug up and the pack's own politics close around it. Victor Madden keeps pressing Eric, opening a rival bar in Shreveport and testing how much humiliation the sheriff will absorb, and Eric has no attention to spare for it while his maker is under his roof.

Alexei breaks loose completely. He kills Eric's day man Bobby Burnham and the vampire Felicia, and Appius finally admits he cannot control his own child. Eric, Pam and the rest of the Shreveport vampires organize a hunt, and Sookie's house at the edge of the woods becomes the place it converges on. Bill, still weak, comes anyway. The buried body is confirmed as Basim al Saud, and the reason for his death lies inside Alcide's pack rather than outside it, which does nothing to make Sookie's land less dangerous while a maddened vampire and a vengeful fairy are both loose in the trees.

The hunt ends in the woods behind Sookie's house in a confused, bloody fight. Alexei is destroyed, and Appius dies of the injuries his own child inflicted, so Eric loses the maker who had unbalanced his whole life and grieves him despite everything. Colman is killed in the same night, ending the vendetta for Claudine. Sookie is injured yet again and left with the aftermath rather than any triumph. Basim's killing is settled inside the werewolf pack: he had been conspiring against Alcide and the pack's enforcer dealt with him, and Sookie's land is finally cleared of it. Bill begins to recover at last. Claude and Dermot stay on in the house, Dermot still not himself, and Sookie ends the book with a household of stranded fairy relatives, a husband whose obligations to his maker are finally over, and Victor Madden still waiting.

characters.description: The Belgian detective summoned to Nasse House by Ariadne Oliver, who cannot explain why the charity fete's staged murder makes her uneasy. He observes the household and the game before a real investigation begins.
characters.name: Hercule Poirot

characters.description: A successful detective novelist hired to design a murder-hunt game for the Nasse House fete. Usually confident in constructing puzzles, she asks Poirot to come because other people's alterations have made the harmless entertainment feel dangerous.
characters.name: Ariadne Oliver

characters.description: The wealthy owner of Nasse House, a forceful self-made man who has restored the estate and indulges his much younger wife. His blunt confidence contrasts with the older family's guarded history.
characters.name: Sir George Stubbs

characters.description: Sir George's striking young wife, widely treated as beautiful, simple, and capricious. Her expensive tastes and apparently childish manner make it difficult to know how much she understands.
characters.name: Hattie Stubbs

characters.description: The widowed former owner of Nasse House, now living quietly in the lodge after her family lost its fortune. She helped arrange Sir George's marriage and remains deeply attached to the estate.
characters.name: Amy Folliat

characters.description: A local girl selected to play the victim in Mrs Oliver's murder hunt. She is observant, fond of gossip, and more interested in payment and small advantages than in the fete's fiction.
characters.name: Marlene Tucker

characters.description: A young man from abroad who says he is Hattie Stubbs's cousin and announces a visit during the fete. The prospect of meeting him produces an unusually strong reaction from Hattie.
characters.name: Etienne de Sousa

characters.description: Sir George's efficient secretary, heavily involved in the practical arrangements for the fete. She regards Lady Stubbs with a mixture of impatience and protective responsibility.
characters.name: Amanda Brewis

characters.description: An architect working on the ornamental folly in the grounds. His plans and movements place him around the estate while preparations for the fete are under way.
characters.name: Michael Weyman

characters.description: A scientist renting a nearby cottage with his wife. Intense and politically preoccupied, he behaves secretively enough to draw attention during the confused events around the fete.
characters.name: Alec Legge

characters.description: Alec Legge's sociable wife, who helps with the fete and is frustrated by her husband's secrecy and isolation. Her movements connect the neighbouring cottage with Nasse House.
characters.name: Sally Legge

characters.description: The police officer who leads the formal inquiry once the fete's staged crime becomes real. He works with Poirot while testing the timelines and movements of visitors across the crowded grounds.
characters.name: Inspector Bland

recaps.ending: Poirot reveals that Sir George Stubbs is really James Folliat, Amy Folliat's son, believed dead after a disreputable past. Amy helped give him a new identity and arranged his marriage to the wealthy Hattie. The woman seen as Lady Stubbs at Nasse House was an accomplice impersonating the real Hattie, who had been killed so James could control her fortune; the real woman's body was concealed beneath the folly. During the fete, the impostor changed clothes and left among the visitors, making Lady Stubbs appear to vanish. Marlene Tucker had learned enough from her grandfather's observations to blackmail Sir George, so he killed her in the boathouse while the murder hunt provided access and confusion. Etienne de Sousa's arrival threatened the impersonation because he knew his true cousin, which forced the conspirators' timetable. Poirot confronts Amy with the consequences of protecting her son. The false Sir George cannot preserve the identity and estate built on the murders, while Amy is left facing the ruin she tried to prevent.
recaps.in_short: Ariadne Oliver asks Poirot to attend a fete at Nasse House because the murder-hunt game she has designed feels as if it is being manipulated for a real purpose. The girl playing the victim, Marlene Tucker, is found strangled in the boathouse, and Lady Hattie Stubbs disappears as her visiting cousin Etienne de Sousa arrives. Poirot eventually connects the crime to the history of the Folliat family and the folly built on the estate. Sir George Stubbs is really James Folliat, Amy Folliat's supposedly dead son. The real, wealthy Hattie was murdered, and another woman had long impersonated her; during the fete the impostor simply changed clothes and departed among the crowd. The real Hattie's body was hidden beneath the folly. Marlene had acquired knowledge that let her blackmail Sir George, so he killed her under cover of the staged game. Etienne's arrival threatened to expose the false Hattie. Poirot's solution leaves Amy Folliat confronting the cost of having protected her son and helped sustain his assumed identity.

recaps.text: Ariadne Oliver abruptly asks Poirot to come to Nasse House, where she has been engaged to devise a murder-hunt game for a charity fete. She cannot name a crime, but repeated suggestions and alterations by other people have made her feel that her fictional plot is being bent toward an unknown purpose. Poirot meets Sir George Stubbs, the wealthy owner; his beautiful young wife Hattie; and Amy Folliat, whose family formerly owned the estate and who now lives at its lodge. The preparations scatter volunteers, guests, and workmen across the house and grounds, creating a setting in which almost anyone can move without attracting notice.

On the day of the fete, visitors crowd Nasse House. Marlene Tucker waits in the boathouse to play the murder victim and reveal the final clue to contestants. Hattie Stubbs is disturbed by the expected arrival of Etienne de Sousa, a cousin from overseas whom she says she barely remembers. Amid games, refreshments, and tours of the grounds, Poirot watches private tensions beneath the public bustle. When the time comes to check the murder hunt, Marlene is found genuinely dead in the boathouse. The staged puzzle has given the killer a reason for the girl to be alone and for people to approach her without immediate alarm.

Inspector Bland takes charge of the crowded crime scene. Hattie Stubbs cannot be found, and her disappearance becomes inseparable from Marlene's death. Etienne de Sousa arrives by river and acknowledges that he has not seen his cousin since she was young, leaving uncertainty about what either would recognise. Witness accounts from the fete produce many movements but few reliable identifications. Marlene seemed an unlikely target, yet her appetite for gossip and small payments suggests she may have possessed information she did not understand. Poirot is dissatisfied with explanations that treat Lady Stubbs simply as another victim or as an impulsive fugitive.

The inquiry examines Marlene's family, including stories repeated by her elderly grandfather, and reconstructs which parts of the grounds could be watched from local paths and cottages. Alec Legge's secretive political concerns and his strained marriage to Sally form one line of suspicion, but they do not explain the design of Mrs Oliver's game. Poirot returns to Amy Folliat and the collapse of her family, including the sons she lost and her role in bringing Sir George and Hattie together. The ornamental folly, an expensive building with little practical use, increasingly matters as a feature imposed on ground with an older history.

Poirot keeps testing the apparent disappearance. A person in distinctive clothes can cease to be noticed simply by changing into the ordinary dress of the fete crowd, while a visitor who knew Hattie only long ago may still threaten a substitution. He concludes that Marlene's murder, Lady Stubbs's absence, and the Folliat past belong to one plan rather than separate events. The girl's knowledge came indirectly from things noticed by an older relative, turning gossip into a basis for blackmail. Poirot also becomes convinced that a death predating the fete is physically tied to the estate and that Amy Folliat knows more than she has admitted about the identity of its present owner.

Poirot identifies Sir George Stubbs as James Folliat, Amy Folliat's son, whose death had been accepted after a troubled past. Amy helped him assume a new life and marry the wealthy Hattie. The real Hattie was murdered, and her body was concealed beneath the folly; an accomplice then impersonated her while James used her wealth as Sir George. At the fete the false Hattie changed into ordinary tourist clothes and left among the visitors, so her disappearance required no abduction. Etienne de Sousa's visit endangered the scheme because he knew the real Hattie, and Marlene Tucker had picked up enough of the hidden history from her grandfather to demand money. Sir George strangled Marlene in the boathouse, using Mrs Oliver's murder hunt to place her alone and to confuse movements around her. Poirot confronts Amy with the crimes enabled by her protection of her son. The assumed identities and the prosperous life at Nasse House collapse under the solution.

characters.description: A telepathic waitress in Bon Temps, married to the vampire Eric Northman by vampire custom and sharing her house with two stranded fairy relatives. She is steadier than she was after her torture but not recovered, increasingly resentful of the blood bond that makes her feelings public property, and tired of being useful to people with more power than she has.
characters.name: Sookie Stackhouse

characters.description: The shapeshifter who owns Merlotte's. Business has never recovered from the public revelation of the two-natured, money is tight, and an attack on the bar is the last thing he can afford. He is still involved with the werewolf enforcer Jannalynn Hopper, a relationship his friends find hard to understand.
characters.name: Sam Merlotte

characters.description: The Viking vampire sheriff of Area Five and Sookie's husband by vampire law. Free of his maker at last, he is being squeezed hard by Victor Madden, the regent Nevada set over Louisiana, who blocks his business, poaches his customers and refuses his people every request. He is angrier than he lets Sookie see.
characters.name: Eric Northman

characters.description: Eric's child and lieutenant, who runs Fangtasia and has never pretended to be anything but ruthless. She has a private reason to hate Victor Madden that she has kept from almost everyone, and it is eating at her.
characters.name: Pam Ravenscroft

characters.description: Sookie's vampire neighbor, recovered from the poisoning that nearly destroyed him and back to full strength. His attachment to Sookie is undiminished and he no longer expects it to be returned; he simply makes himself available when she needs someone she can rely on.
characters.name: Bill Compton

characters.description: Sookie's part-fairy cousin, lodging in her house since Faery closed and running a strip club in Monroe that has become a refuge for the other fae stranded on this side. Vain, blunt and affectionate in his own way, he keeps his real plans to himself.
characters.name: Claude Crane

characters.description: Sookie's great-uncle, a fairy who looks like Jason's twin and lives in her attic. He is helpful, hard-working and plainly not in full possession of himself, and Sookie has come to believe that something was deliberately done to his mind.
characters.name: Dermot Brigant

characters.description: Felipe de Castro's regent in Louisiana, based in Shreveport and set over Eric. Unfailingly pleasant, he has spent months obstructing Eric in every way that stops short of open attack, and both sides know an accommodation is no longer possible.
characters.name: Victor Madden

characters.description: Packmaster of the Shreveport werewolves, who has decided that binding Sookie to his pack is worth almost any tactic. His judgment about her, and about what she owes him, has been poor for some time.
characters.name: Alcide Herveaux

characters.description: The Long Tooth pack's enforcer and Sam's girlfriend, small, expensively dressed and genuinely dangerous. Her devotion to the pack outweighs everything else she claims to care about.
characters.name: Jannalynn Hopper

characters.description: A Shreveport hairdresser and a friend of Pam's, calm and observant, who moves easily between the human and vampire worlds. His sister Miriam is seriously ill.
characters.name: Immanuel Earnest

characters.description: Immanuel's sister and Pam's lover, dying of leukemia. Vampire law requires a regent's permission before anyone may be turned, and permission has been refused.
characters.name: Miriam Earnest

characters.description: Eric's day man, a werewolf who goes by a name he chose for himself and handles the daylight business Eric cannot. Guarded, professional, and firm about the difference between the work and his private life.
characters.name: Mustapha Khan

characters.description: A young human who works around the vampires of Shreveport and has a personal grievance against Victor Madden over a family death. He is willing to take risks that a sensible person would not.
characters.name: Colton

characters.description: The younger sister of Debbie Pelt, the shapeshifter who vanished after trying to kill Sookie. She has spent years insisting that Sookie is responsible and has been ordered by her own kind to leave the matter alone.
characters.name: Sandra Pelt

characters.description: The vampire queen of Oklahoma, who does not appear in person. Her name surfaces in old documents belonging to Eric's dead maker, in terms that concern Eric's future rather than his past.
characters.name: Freyda

recaps.ending: Eric and Pam's conspiracy succeeds: Victor Madden and his entourage are lured to Fangtasia after hours and killed there, with Sookie, Bill, Mustapha, Colton, Immanuel and the Shreveport vampires all taking part. The killing is concealed rather than confessed, so Eric holds Area Five with Felipe de Castro's regent gone and the certainty that the king will eventually ask questions. Pam has lost Miriam, who died before permission to turn her ever came, and her grief is what drove the whole plot. Sandra Pelt's campaign against Sookie is broken and she is taken out of circulation, though nobody expects her to stay quiet forever. In the attic, Sookie has found her grandmother's letter and learned that her real grandfather was the fairy Fintan, along with the gift he left: a cluviel dor, a fairy love token that will grant its holder one wish, which she tells almost no one about. Dermot's curse is broken and he is himself again. The book closes on a document Sookie was never meant to see: Eric's dead maker pledged him in marriage to Freyda, the vampire queen of Oklahoma, an obligation Eric has known about and not mentioned, and which neither of them can simply refuse.
recaps.in_short: Someone throws a firebomb into Merlotte's, and Sookie's attempt to find out why runs into an old enemy's vendetta. At the same time Eric and Pam decide they can no longer live under Victor Madden, the regent Nevada placed over Louisiana, who has spent months strangling Eric's business and who refused Pam permission to turn her dying lover Miriam. Sookie is drawn into the conspiracy against him. Clearing out her attic with her fairy cousins Claude and Dermot, she finds a letter from her grandmother revealing that her real grandfather was the fairy Fintan, and with it a cluviel dor, a fairy token that grants one wish to whoever holds it. Dermot's curse is broken by a ritual the three of them perform. The plot against Victor comes to a head at Fangtasia, where he and his people are ambushed and destroyed. In the aftermath Sookie discovers papers showing that Eric's dead maker promised him in marriage to the vampire queen of Oklahoma.

recaps.text: Sookie Stackhouse is a telepathic waitress in Bon Temps, Louisiana, where vampires and shapeshifters are both public knowledge. Louisiana was conquered by Felipe de Castro of Nevada, whose regent Victor Madden now sits over Eric Northman, the vampire sheriff Sookie is married to by vampire custom and bound to by exchanged blood. Sookie is part fairy: her great-grandfather, Prince Niall Brigant, fought a war against a faction that wanted his human-blooded descendants dead, during which Sookie was abducted and tortured, her fairy godmother Claudine was killed, and Bill Compton was poisoned rescuing her. Niall then closed Faery for good, stranding part-fairies including Sookie's cousin Claude and her great-uncle Dermot, who now live in her house; Dermot's mind has been tampered with. Eric's maker recently arrived with a second, damaged child, and the visit ended with both of them destroyed. Sookie's brother Jason is a widower, and Sookie is quietly teaching her small telepathic cousin Hunter how to manage his gift.

Someone throws a firebomb through the window at Merlotte's during business hours. The damage is contained and nobody is killed, but Sam cannot absorb the loss and the attack looks deliberate rather than random. Sookie helps with the cleanup and starts listening to what the parish is thinking, on the assumption that an arsonist in a small town rarely keeps it to himself. Her home life is crowded: Claude has settled in permanently and Dermot is living in the attic, still not himself and still working through the accumulated contents of four generations of Stackhouses. Alcide Herveaux turns up uninvited and in no clothes, a clumsy attempt to tie Sookie to his pack that leaves her angrier with him than she has ever been.

The investigation into the fire makes slow progress, and Sookie begins to suspect the target was her rather than Sam. In Shreveport, Eric's position under Victor Madden has become intolerable: the regent has opened a competing club, blocked Eric's ventures and refused every request his people make, all with unbroken good humor. Pam is more openly furious than her maker, and Sookie learns why. Pam's lover Miriam Earnest is dying of leukemia, and only a regent may authorize a new vampire being made; Victor has refused, and goes on refusing. Sookie also starts to work through the attic in earnest with Dermot, sorting a century of family belongings she has never had the heart to touch.

Eric and Pam stop talking about tolerating Victor and start planning to kill him, which under vampire law is treason against Felipe de Castro unless it is never discovered. They assemble people with reasons of their own: Bill, Eric's day man Mustapha Khan, Immanuel Earnest, and Colton, a young man who blames Victor for a death in his family. Sookie is brought in because her telepathy can tell them what Victor's human staff know. Meanwhile the trail from the firebombing leads back to Sandra Pelt, the sister of Debbie Pelt, who has never stopped believing Sookie killed her and has been hiring people to make Sookie's life dangerous.

Sandra Pelt's campaign escalates from arson to direct attempts on Sookie, and dealing with her runs alongside everything else. Sookie, Claude and Dermot perform a fairy ritual intended to break whatever was done to Dermot's mind, and it works: he becomes coherent, purposeful and grateful, and remembers who cursed him and why. The plan against Victor takes shape around a pretext he cannot refuse, an occasion at Fangtasia after closing that will put him and his guards inside Eric's own building with limited numbers. Pam presses for it hardest, because Miriam's time is running out and Victor's permission is never going to come.

Sorting the attic, Sookie finds a letter her grandmother left her and learns the truth behind her own family: Adele Stackhouse's children were fathered not by her husband but by Fintan, a half-fairy and Niall's son, which is where Sookie's blood and her telepathy come from. With the letter is a hidden object, a cluviel dor, a fairy love token that will grant one wish to the person holding it. Sookie keeps it, tells almost nobody, and understands that if the vampires learn of it she will never be allowed to keep it. Miriam dies without ever being turned. The plan for Fangtasia is finalized, every participant briefed, and the trap set for a night when Victor will come with only as many guards as courtesy allows.

Victor Madden and his entourage walk into Fangtasia after hours and are attacked by everyone Eric has assembled. The fight is close, protracted and expensive, and Sookie is in it rather than watching; when it ends, Victor and all of his people are dead and the bodies are disposed of so that nothing can be proved. Eric holds Area Five outright for the first time since the conquest, with the knowledge that Felipe de Castro will eventually come asking what became of his regent. Pam has her revenge and nothing else, Miriam being already dead. Sandra Pelt's vendetta is broken and she is put out of the way. Dermot, restored to himself, stays on. And in the papers left behind by Eric's dead maker Sookie finds a contract: Appius pledged Eric in marriage to Freyda, the vampire queen of Oklahoma, an arrangement Eric knew about and never mentioned to her.

characters.description: A polished traveler of middling rank who arrives in a provincial town with two servants and no obvious business. He carefully flatters officials and landowners, gathering information about their estates while presenting himself as respectable, agreeable, and unremarkable.
characters.name: Pavel Ivanovich Chichikov

characters.description: Chichikov's coachman, responsible for the britzka and its three horses. He is sociable, frequently careless, and prone to drinking, and his uncertain sense of direction repeatedly shapes his master's travels between estates.
characters.name: Selifan

characters.description: Chichikov's taciturn valet. Petrushka wears a distinctive old coat, reads without much concern for meaning, and brings his own habits and atmosphere into the rooms he prepares for his master.
characters.name: Petrushka

characters.description: A sentimental landowner whose refined phrases and plans for improvements never become practical action. He welcomes Chichikov with elaborate warmth and is the first person from whom Chichikov asks to acquire serfs who remain on the tax register although they have died.
characters.name: Manilov

characters.description: A widowed landowner who gives Chichikov shelter after he loses the road in a storm. Practical but deeply cautious about any unfamiliar bargain, she fears selling too cheaply and treats deceased serfs as another commodity whose market price she may not understand.
characters.name: Korobochka

characters.description: A noisy, impulsive landowner and compulsive gambler whom Chichikov meets again at an inn. Nozdryov lies, boasts, quarrels, and tries to turn every transaction into a game or an exchange on his own terms, making him dangerous to a scheme that depends on discretion.
characters.name: Nozdryov

characters.description: A heavy, blunt landowner whose solid house and possessions resemble his own practical temperament. Unlike Chichikov's more dreamy or erratic hosts, he immediately treats the proposed transfer of dead serfs as hard bargaining and praises each deceased worker as valuable property.
characters.name: Sobakevich

characters.description: A once-prosperous landowner whose miserliness has reduced his estate and household to decay. Suspicious of everyone and unable to use what he hoards, he nevertheless has many dead or runaway serfs still burdening his tax register, making him especially receptive to Chichikov's offer.
characters.name: Plyushkin

characters.description: The provincial governor's young daughter, recently returned from her education and conspicuous to Chichikov at a ball. His attention to her disrupts the careful social performance by which he has won the town's approval.
characters.name: The governor's daughter

characters.description: An army veteran whose history is told by the postmaster as a proposed explanation for Chichikov's identity. After losing an arm and a leg in war, Kopeikin seeks government help in the capital but encounters delay and indifference.
characters.name: Captain Kopeikin

characters.description: An educated landowner encountered when Chichikov resumes his travels. Tentetnikov has withdrawn to his estate after disappointed ambitions and fallen into inactivity, though his attachment to General Betrishchev's daughter still connects him to neighboring society.
characters.name: Andrei Ivanovich Tentetnikov

characters.description: A proud, imposing landowner and retired general who has quarreled with Tentetnikov. Chichikov seeks his favor and tries to use the estrangement, and the general's affection for his daughter, as openings for new social and financial maneuvers.
characters.name: General Betrishchev

characters.description: General Betrishchev's spirited daughter and the woman Tentetnikov loves. Her presence gives emotional weight to the estrangement between the two men and to Chichikov's attempt to present himself as their useful intermediary.
characters.name: Ulinka

characters.description: A wealthy, energetic estate manager whose productive farming and disciplined household contrast with the neglect found elsewhere. Chichikov is impressed by the profits that practical work can produce, though he remains more attracted to shortcuts than to sustained reform.
characters.name: Kostanzhoglo

characters.description: A bankrupt gentleman whose neglected estate is offered for sale. Generous impulses and disorderly spending have left him unable to support his large household, and his distress creates another opportunity for Chichikov to acquire property through borrowed money and advantageous paperwork.
characters.name: Khlobuev

characters.description: A rich, influential man with a reputation for moral seriousness and direct speech. When Chichikov's renewed dealings bring him into grave legal danger, Murazov urges him to abandon fraud and redirect his abilities toward an honest life.
characters.name: Murazov

recaps.ending: The surviving second part does not provide a completed ending. After returning to schemes involving land, credit, and official documents, Chichikov becomes entangled in a serious forgery case and is arrested under a newly severe governor-general. In confinement he is stripped of the signs of prosperity on which his identity depends and despairs over the collapse of his position. Murazov visits him, identifies his talent and persistence as qualities wasted on fraud, and presses him to make a genuine moral change. Murazov also appeals to the authorities, while other officials continue trying to manipulate the case for money and advantage. The extant manuscript breaks off amid these efforts, with Chichikov's legal fate and promised reform unresolved. Gogol destroyed much of the continuation, so the intended completion of Chichikov's journey and the broader design of the poem cannot be recovered from the text that remains.
recaps.in_short: Pavel Chichikov arrives in a provincial town and charms its officials before visiting nearby landowners with an unusual offer: he will take legal ownership of serfs who have died since the last census but remain taxable on paper. Manilov gives them away, Korobochka sells cautiously, Nozdryov disrupts the scheme, Sobakevich bargains, and the miser Plyushkin gladly transfers many names. Chichikov plans to use these paper holdings as security and present himself as wealthy. Rumor first makes him a celebrated landowner, then turns against him when his dealings are exposed and wild theories spread about his identity; he flees. His history reveals a career built on ingratiation, accumulation, and official fraud. In the unfinished second part he resumes schemes among another group of landowners, is drawn into forged documents, and is arrested. The moralist Murazov urges him to reform, but the surviving manuscript ends before either his legal case or his moral future is settled.

recaps.text: Pavel Ivanovich Chichikov arrives in an unnamed provincial capital with his coachman Selifan and valet Petrushka. He quickly calls on the governor and other leading officials, praising each man and avoiding firm statements about his own purpose. His careful manners win invitations to dinners and a ball, where he meets several landowners. He first visits Manilov, a pleasant but idle estate owner given to vague ideals. Chichikov finally reveals his business: he wants the legal names of male serfs who have died since the last census but remain registered, leaving their owners liable for taxes. Because the transaction would relieve him of a useless burden, Manilov agrees to transfer the names without payment and treats the bargain as an act of friendship. Chichikov leaves with the first group of the paper property he calls dead souls.

After Selifan loses the road during a storm, Chichikov spends the night at the estate of the widow Korobochka. She understands ordinary farm goods but is alarmed by the novelty of selling the names of dead serfs. Chichikov alternates explanations, pressure, and promises of future business until she agrees, though she remains worried that she has accepted too little. At an inn he encounters Nozdryov, a boastful gambler who drags him home. Nozdryov refuses a straightforward sale and tries to attach the dead souls to unwanted horses, dogs, and games of chance. When Chichikov will not cooperate, their quarrel nearly becomes violent before an official arrives on another matter. Chichikov escapes without a purchase, but Nozdryov now knows enough to threaten the secrecy of the plan.

Chichikov next bargains with Sobakevich, a blunt and calculating landowner. Sobakevich immediately recognizes that Chichikov expects some benefit and demands payment, describing each deceased serf's trade and virtues as if the man were still marketable. They eventually agree on a price and carefully record the names. From him Chichikov learns about Plyushkin, an extremely rich landowner whose miserliness has ruined his estate. Plyushkin hoards worthless scraps while food and buildings decay, and many of his serfs have died or run away. Because he still owes taxes on them, he gladly lets Chichikov assume the registered dead and also sells him the names of runaways. Chichikov returns to town pleased with a substantial list acquired through a mixture of gifts and purchases.

Chichikov and the officials complete deeds that make his purchases appear to be an ordinary transfer of living serfs for resettlement elsewhere. At the ensuing celebration, the town treats him as a substantial proprietor and speculates approvingly about his fortune and marriage prospects. The attention expands into social enthusiasm, particularly among the town's women. At the governor's ball Chichikov becomes absorbed in the governor's young daughter and neglects the admirers whose approval helped establish him. Nozdryov then loudly asks him about the dead souls, confusing the guests and giving the first public clue that the transactions are not what they seem. Chichikov leaves angry, while Korobochka reaches town to discover whether other buyers would have paid more, bringing another threat to his carefully managed reputation.

Korobochka's inquiries and Nozdryov's talk set off a wave of rumor.
