The town combines Chichikov's secret purchases with his attention to the governor's daughter, producing theories that he plans an abduction or is a dangerous criminal in disguise. Officials who once welcomed him become frightened that an inspection or scandal will expose their own misconduct. Their conference generates increasingly implausible guesses, including the postmaster's tale of the disabled Captain Kopeikin, until the strain contributes to the prosecutor's sudden death. Chichikov, recovering from illness and initially unaware of the change, finds doors closed to him. Nozdryov finally tells him the circulating stories. He leaves town hurriedly. The narrative then gives his history: trained from childhood to save money and please superiors, Chichikov repeatedly advanced through charm and corrupt ventures, lost his gains when schemes were exposed, and devised the dead-souls plan as his next route to wealth.

In the surviving continuation, Chichikov reappears on the estate of Andrei Tentetnikov, an educated man whose early hopes have given way to isolation and inactivity. Tentetnikov is estranged from the neighboring General Betrishchev but remains attached to the general's daughter, Ulina. Chichikov presents himself as a possible reconciler and wins access to the general through flattery and invented family business. He moves among a new set of estates, adapting his story to each household and seeking property and registered souls that can restore his fortunes. The social world has changed, but his method remains the same: identify another person's vanity, grievance, boredom, or need, then make himself appear useful to it.

Chichikov encounters sharp contrasts among the later landowners. Kostanzhoglo runs a productive estate through close attention and work, while the generous but disorderly Khlobuev has driven his property toward sale. Chichikov admires the profits of honest management but tries to acquire opportunity through loans, influence, and documents rather than adopting its discipline. His renewed maneuvers eventually involve a forged will and competing officials, and a new governor-general's campaign against corruption places him under arrest. In confinement Chichikov loses the clothes, possessions, and public standing that sustained his self-image. The wealthy moralist Murazov urges him to recognize that his energy and adaptability could serve a life other than fraud and attempts to obtain mercy, while corrupt intermediaries continue seeking advantage from the case. The manuscript breaks off before the prosecution, Murazov's intervention, or Chichikov's promised reform reaches a resolution; the novel's second part survives only in incomplete form.

characters.description: A telepathic waitress at Merlotte's bar in Bon Temps, Louisiana, single again after ending her relationship with the vampire Bill Compton and trying hard to have an ordinary winter. She owns her grandmother's house, works doubles, and has learned to charge the supernatural community for her services. She still hears every mind around her, which makes solitude a relief rather than a punishment.
characters.name: Sookie Stackhouse

characters.description: The thousand-year-old Norse vampire who owns Fangtasia and rules the vampires of northern Louisiana. Sookie finds him on a dark road on New Year's Eve, barefoot and half dressed, with no memory of who or what he is beyond the fact that he is a vampire. Stripped of a millennium of calculation, he is gentle, affectionate and frightened, and nothing like the man who has spent two years maneuvering her into his debt.
characters.name: Eric Northman

characters.description: Sookie's former lover, the Bon Temps vampire who lives across the cemetery from her. He leaves the country at the start of the book on research of his own, and their dealings are polite, painful and brief.
characters.name: Bill Compton

characters.description: Sookie's brother, now a road crew supervisor in Bon Temps and involved with a young woman from the isolated crossroads community of Hotshot. He disappears from his own house in the first days of the year, leaving blood on the dock behind it and no other trace.
characters.name: Jason Stackhouse

characters.description: Sookie's boss at Merlotte's and a shapeshifter. He keeps the bar running, keeps her secrets, and does what he can to help find Jason, while making no secret of wishing she would stay out of vampire business.
characters.name: Sam Merlotte

characters.description: Eric's second at Fangtasia and the vampire who has to run northern Louisiana while its sheriff is missing. Practical and cold-blooded about the crisis, she is the one who negotiates with Sookie to hide Eric, and who names the price.
characters.name: Pam

characters.description: The tattooed vampire who tends bar at Fangtasia. With Eric gone he shares the running of the territory with Pam, and he is less inclined than she is to spend vampire money on a human's protection.
characters.name: Chow

characters.description: A young woman from Hotshot, a closed rural community outside Bon Temps whose families keep to themselves and marry among themselves. She has been seeing Jason Stackhouse, and she is one of the last people to have been with him before he disappeared.
characters.name: Crystal Norris

characters.description: A waitress at Merlotte's, a divorced mother with a young son, who practices Wicca with a small local circle. She is uneasy about being asked to help with vampire business, but she knows which witches are ordinary practitioners and which are something else.
characters.name: Holly Cleary

characters.description: The head of the Hotshot community, a road crew foreman and a werepanther. Courteous, watchful and openly interested in Sookie, he offers his people's help in the search for Jason and expects the favor to be remembered.
characters.name: Calvin Norris

characters.description: The leader of a coven that has come to Shreveport demanding a share of the vampires' businesses. Her witches are not ordinary Wiccans: they are also werewolves, and they drink vampire blood, which makes their magic far stronger than it should be. She is the reason the sheriff of the area is wandering the roads with no memory.
characters.name: Hallow Stonebrook

characters.description: Hallow's brother and second in the coven, a witch and werewolf who handles the violence her plans require.
characters.name: Mark Stonebrook

characters.description: The Shreveport werewolf who escorted Sookie to Jackson the year before, now running his family's surveying business and free of his engagement. His pack is drawn into the fight against the coven, and he and Sookie remain on cautious, friendly terms.
characters.name: Alcide Herveaux

characters.description: The leader of the Shreveport werewolf pack, a retired air force officer who runs pack business like a command. He negotiates the alliance with the vampires against the coven and expects discipline from everyone involved.
characters.name: Colonel Flood

characters.description: A tall, black-haired woman of striking beauty who appears at Sookie's side when the fighting starts, announces that she is looking after her, and will not explain much beyond that. She is not human, she is not a shapeshifter or a vampire, and she is unwilling to be anywhere near iron or lemons.
characters.name: Claudine

characters.description: The Jackson shapeshifter who was cast out by Alcide Herveaux for trying to get Sookie killed in Mississippi. Publicly disgraced and blaming Sookie for it, she has not let the matter drop.
characters.name: Debbie Pelt

recaps.ending: The alliance of vampires, werewolves and local Wiccans destroys Hallow Stonebrook's coven in a running fight at their hideout. Mark Stonebrook is killed, Hallow is taken alive, and she is made to undo the spell she cast. Before that happens, Debbie Pelt lets herself into Sookie's house with a rifle. She shoots at Sookie and hits Eric, who puts himself in the way, and Sookie kills her with a shotgun. Eric disposes of the body and the truck so completely that no one will ever find them, and the two of them agree to say nothing. Then the curse is broken. Eric wakes as himself, with his thousand years and his calculation restored, and remembers nothing at all of the weeks he spent in Sookie's house: not their nights together, not the fighting, and not Debbie Pelt. He goes back to Shreveport as the sheriff he was, pays Sookie what he owes her, and is baffled by whatever it is she will not say. Jason is found alive, dumped near his own house after being held and bitten repeatedly by a werepanther, and he will change at the next full moon whether he wants to or not; who took him is still unknown. Sookie is left with a brother turning into something he did not choose, a killing nobody knows about but her, and a memory of Eric that only she carries.
recaps.in_short: Driving home on New Year's Eve, Sookie finds Eric Northman running down a dark road half naked with no memory of who he is, cursed by a coven of witches who are also werewolves and who want a share of his businesses. Pam pays Sookie to hide him at her house, where an unguarded and affectionate Eric becomes her lover. At the same time Sookie's brother Jason vanishes from his home, and the trail leads toward the closed werepanther community of Hotshot. Sookie's telepathy helps a coalition of vampires, werewolves and local Wiccans find and destroy the coven, killing Hallow Stonebrook's brother and taking Hallow alive to lift the curse. On the same night, Debbie Pelt breaks into Sookie's house to kill her, wounds Eric, and is shot dead by Sookie; Eric makes the body disappear. When the curse breaks, Eric returns to himself with no memory of any of it, including the killing and the weeks with Sookie. Jason is found alive but bitten, and will become a werepanther at the next full moon.

recaps.text: Sookie Stackhouse is a telepathic waitress at Merlotte's bar in Bon Temps, Louisiana, in a world where vampires live openly among humans. Her grandmother was murdered by a killer who was really hunting Sookie, and Sookie herself has twice been nearly killed for vampire business. Her boss Sam Merlotte is a shapeshifter; the parish has been visited by a maenad; and she has been held prisoner by the anti-vampire Fellowship of the Sun in Dallas. Her relationship with Bill Compton, the vampire who came home to Bon Temps, is over: he had been planning to leave her for Lorena, the vampire who made him, before he was kidnapped and tortured in Mississippi, and when Sookie rescued him he nearly killed her while out of his mind with hunger. She killed Lorena herself. She also came away with the database of vampires Bill had been compiling for the Queen of Louisiana, which she keeps hidden as leverage. All of this is watched over by Eric Northman, the thousand-year-old Norse vampire who rules the area from his Shreveport bar and who wants Sookie for reasons he has never bothered to disguise. In Jackson she met the werewolf Alcide Herveaux, whose ex-lover Debbie Pelt tried to have her killed and was cast out of decent society for it.

Sookie works New Year's Eve at Merlotte's, newly single and determined to be dull for a while. Bill leaves the country on research of his own, which suits her. Driving home in the early hours she nearly hits a man running down the road in the cold: Eric Northman, barefoot, half dressed, and with no memory of anything except that he is a vampire. She takes him in. Pam and Chow arrive with the explanation. A coven has come to Shreveport demanding a cut of the vampires' businesses, and its witches are not ordinary practitioners: they are werewolves who drink vampire blood, which makes their magic strong enough to strip a thousand-year-old sheriff of his mind and set him wandering. Until the coven can be found and the curse broken, Eric has to be hidden somewhere no vampire would think to look, and Pam offers Sookie money to keep him at her house. Sookie takes the job.

Living with Eric is nothing like knowing him. Without a millennium of scheming he is warm, direct, easily hurt and completely dependent on her, and Sookie finds herself protecting him. Then her brother Jason vanishes. His truck is at his house, the door is open, and there is blood on the dock over the pond behind it. The police can do nothing with it. Sookie learns that Jason had been seeing Crystal Norris, a young woman from Hotshot, an isolated crossroads community whose families never marry outsiders, and that Crystal's account of the night is a lie. Sookie goes to Hotshot herself and finds a community of werepanthers, headed by Calvin Norris, who offers his people's help in the search and makes plain that he would like Sookie for himself. Nobody in Hotshot will say what happened to her brother.

Sookie is pulled in two directions: hunting for Jason and being paid to hide Eric while the vampires hunt the coven. Fangtasia's people are outmatched and know it, and the coven has begun killing. To find Hallow Stonebrook and her brother Mark, the vampires make an alliance with the Shreveport werewolf pack under Colonel Flood, with Alcide Herveaux among them, and with a circle of local Wiccans who want nothing to do with either side but are more afraid of Hallow. Sookie's telepathy is what makes the alliance work, since she can read the human minds around the coven's operation. She and Eric become lovers during the days he is hidden with her, an intimacy neither of them could have had otherwise, and she is clear-eyed that it will not survive the return of his memory.

The coalition locates the coven's hideout and attacks. The fight is bloody and one-sided in both directions by turns, since the witches are werewolves with vampire blood in them, and both the pack and the vampires take losses. Sookie is in the middle of it and is guarded by a tall, striking woman who appears from nowhere, introduces herself as Claudine, says she is there to look after Sookie, and refuses to explain what she is beyond being neither vampire nor shifter. Mark Stonebrook is killed. Hallow is taken alive rather than destroyed, because she is the only one who can undo what she did to Eric, and the vampires' methods for persuading her are not ones Sookie wants described to her.

That same night, Debbie Pelt lets herself into Sookie's house with a rifle. Cast out by Alcide and disgraced in front of everyone she cares about, she blames Sookie and has come to finish it. She fires, and Eric puts himself between them and takes the bullet. Sookie kills her with a shotgun. Eric, still without his memory but entirely competent, disposes of the body and Debbie's truck so thoroughly that they will never be found, and the two of them agree that nobody else will ever know. Sookie is left with a death on her conscience and no one she can tell. Then Hallow is made to lift the curse, and Eric's thousand years come back to him.

Eric wakes as himself and remembers nothing of the weeks he spent in Sookie's house: not their nights together, not the alliance, not Debbie Pelt bleeding on her kitchen floor. He returns to Shreveport as the sheriff he always was, pays Sookie generously for hiding him, and is left plainly aware that something happened that she will not discuss. Sookie decides not to tell him. Jason is found alive, dumped near his own house after weeks of being held in a shed and bitten repeatedly by a werepanther; whoever took him is still unidentified, and Jason will change at the next full moon whether he chooses to or not, without the strength or the standing of a panther born to it. Sookie ends the book with her brother permanently altered, a killing that only she remembers, and a private history with Eric Northman that he does not know he has.

characters.description: A waitress in her mid-twenties at Merlotte's bar in the small northern Louisiana town of Bon Temps. She has been able to hear other people's thoughts since childhood, a talent she calls her disability and hides as best she can; the town has settled on treating her as simple. She lives with her grandmother in the old family house, swims and sunbathes to keep some pleasure in her life, and has never managed a normal relationship because she always knows what a man is thinking. The public existence of vampires, revealed a couple of years earlier once a synthetic blood made it possible for them to live openly, fascinates her, and she has been waiting for one to walk into the bar.
characters.name: Sookie Stackhouse

characters.description: A vampire who has returned to Bon Temps to claim the house his family left him across the cemetery from the Stackhouse place. He was born in the area, fought in the Civil War, and did not come home from it as a living man. Courteous, old-fashioned, and deliberately mainstreaming into human society now that vampires are public, he drinks bottled synthetic blood and wants to be accepted as a taxpaying resident. Sookie is drawn to him above all because his mind is completely silent to her, which is the first rest she has ever had in company.
characters.name: Bill Compton

characters.description: The owner of Merlotte's bar and grill and Sookie's boss for several years. He is a compact, red-gold-haired man who arrived in Bon Temps from somewhere else, keeps his private life entirely to himself, and lives in a trailer behind his own bar. He looks out for Sookie, is plainly attracted to her, and disapproves of her interest in vampires. Sookie has never been able to read him properly: where other minds give her words and pictures, his gives her a shifting blur she cannot settle on.
characters.name: Sam Merlotte

characters.description: Sookie's older brother, who works for the parish road crew and has inherited the family house's other half of trouble. Good-looking, vain, and constantly involved with women, he treats Bon Temps as his personal hunting ground and has slept with a great many of the local waitresses and barflies. He and Sookie love each other but scrape against each other constantly; he has never been comfortable with her telepathy.
characters.name: Jason Stackhouse

characters.description: Sookie and Jason's grandmother, who raised them both after their parents drowned in a flash flood when Sookie was seven. She is elderly, sharp, endlessly busy, and unembarrassed by her granddaughter's gift. She belongs to the Descendants of the Glorious Dead, a local club devoted to Civil War history, and is delighted at the idea of a genuine veteran of that war living down the road.
characters.name: Adele Stackhouse

characters.description: A red-haired waitress at Merlotte's, several times married and currently between husbands, with two small children. She is Sookie's closest friend at work, warm and gossipy, and comfortable with Sookie in a way most of the town is not.
characters.name: Arlene Fowler

characters.description: The short-order cook at Merlotte's, a flamboyant Black man who wears makeup and bright nail polish and takes obvious pleasure in unsettling the bar's more conventional customers. He is a good cook, an unreliable employee, and one of the few people in Bon Temps who does not treat Sookie as damaged.
characters.name: Lafayette Reynold

characters.description: A waitress at Merlotte's who works the shift opposite Sookie's. She has a taste for rough company and for men who will hurt her a little, and she has been seen with vampires. She and Sookie have never liked each other much.
characters.name: Dawn Green

characters.description: A detective with the Bon Temps police, from an old local family that has come down in the world. He is stubborn, not stupid, and openly suspicious of Jason Stackhouse once the local women start turning up dead. Sookie has known him and his sister Portia all her life.
characters.name: Andy Bellefleur

characters.description: A member of the parish road crew alongside Jason and one of Arlene's former husbands. He is a small, wiry Cajun with a thick accent that comes and goes, an easy manner with women, and a habit of turning up wherever people are talking. He remains friendly with Arlene and is around her children often.
characters.name: Rene Lenier

characters.description: A vampire well over a thousand years old, Norse by origin, tall and blond and openly amused by almost everything. He owns Fangtasia, a vampire bar in Shreveport built to sell the experience of vampires to tourists, and holds authority over the vampires of the surrounding territory, Bill included. He is immediately interested in Sookie once he learns what she can do, and treats that interest as a claim.
characters.name: Eric Northman

characters.description: Eric's second at Fangtasia, a blonde vampire who works the door in a trailing black gown as part of the bar's act and is far more practical than the costume suggests. She is dry, direct, and unbothered by human feeling, and she takes a certain liking to Sookie.
characters.name: Pam

characters.description: A vampire made from a famous singer whose body was taken from a morgue by an admiring attendant. The change went wrong because he was already too far gone, leaving him simple, unpredictable, and prone to violence if startled. Other vampires keep him quietly employed, never speak his human name in front of him, and call him Bubba; he prefers the blood of cats to anything bottled.
characters.name: Bubba

recaps.ending: Sookie catches the truth out of another mind: the killer is Rene Lenier, Arlene's former husband and Jason's workmate. His own sister took a vampire lover, and he strangled her for it; since then he has killed local women who did the same. Maudette Pickens and Dawn Green died that way, and Sookie's grandmother died in Sookie's place, because Sookie was the woman in Bon Temps sleeping with a vampire. Rene attacks her, and she survives the assault only barely, badly injured; he is stopped, and Sookie is healed by being given vampire blood. Two things about her life are permanently changed by the night. Sam Merlotte turns out to be a shapeshifter: the stray collie that has been sleeping at her house was her boss, keeping watch over her. And the vampire world now knows exactly what she can do. Jason is cleared of the murders and released, but he is still on the wrong side of his sister and taking vampire blood as a drug. Bill returns from vampire business in New Orleans having taken on a formal position among his own kind, which will pull him away from Bon Temps more and more. Sookie is left with her grandmother's house, a vampire lover, and no way back to an ordinary life.
recaps.in_short: In small-town Bon Temps, Louisiana, telepathic barmaid Sookie Stackhouse falls for Bill Compton, a Civil War veteran turned vampire who has come home to claim his family's house, and whose mind is blessedly silent to her. Their courtship runs alongside a string of stranglings: local women who have slept with vampires are being murdered, and Sookie's womanizing brother Jason, who knew several of them, becomes the sheriff's favorite suspect. Sookie's grandmother is killed in the family kitchen, apparently in Sookie's place. Bill introduces Sookie to the vampires of Shreveport, including the ancient Eric Northman, who quickly finds uses for her gift. Reading a stray memory, Sookie realizes the murderer is Rene Lenier, who began by killing his own sister for taking a vampire lover. He nearly kills her before he is stopped, and she is saved by vampire blood. In the process she learns that her boss, Sam Merlotte, is a shapeshifter, and that her town has always held far more than she knew.

recaps.text: Sookie Stackhouse waits tables at Merlotte's bar in Bon Temps, a small town in northern Louisiana. She has been telepathic since childhood, hides it as well as she can, and is generally written off locally as slow. Vampires revealed themselves to the world two years earlier, once a synthetic blood made it possible for them to live without preying on people, and Sookie has been hoping one would come to Bon Temps. When Bill Compton walks into the bar she is delighted to discover that his mind gives her nothing at all. She follows a rough couple called the Rattrays outside and interrupts them draining Bill's blood, which sells at high prices as a drug. Days later the Rattrays catch her alone in the parking lot and beat her nearly to death; Bill drives them off and heals her by making her drink his blood. In the background, a local woman named Maudette Pickens has been found strangled in her apartment. She had been known to keep company with vampires, and Sookie's brother Jason had been with her, which draws the attention of the Bon Temps police.

The Rattrays die when their trailer is torn apart in what is officially recorded as a freak tornado, and Sookie understands well enough what really happened. Bill begins courting her in his formal, old-fashioned way and starts restoring his inherited house across the cemetery. Sookie's grandmother, delighted to have a genuine Civil War veteran nearby, persuades Bill to address the Descendants of the Glorious Dead, and he speaks to a packed room about the war and the men he served with. Then Dawn Green, the other Merlotte's waitress, is found strangled in her bedroom. Both dead women had slept with vampires and both had slept with Jason, and he had made videotapes with them, so Andy Bellefleur and the parish sheriff pull him in for questioning repeatedly. Jason turns on Sookie for her relationship with Bill, and the town's mood toward vampires curdles. Sookie, in love and out of her depth, has to decide how far she is willing to go into Bill's world.

Bill takes Sookie to Fangtasia, a vampire bar in Shreveport, to ask whether any local vampire knew the murdered women. There she meets Eric Northman, who is more than a thousand years old and holds authority over the vampires of the area, and his second, Pam. When Sookie picks up an impending police raid from a mind in the room and warns Eric in time, she reveals her ability to exactly the people she should have hidden it from, and Eric marks her as a resource he intends to use. Worse follows at home: Sookie comes back to the house to find that her grandmother has been strangled in the kitchen. Gran had taken over an evening Sookie was expected to be home for, and the town and Sookie both understand that the killer had come for Sookie, the one woman in Bon Temps openly seeing a vampire. Jason, wild with grief, blames his sister at the funeral.

Gran leaves Sookie the house, and Sookie goes on alone in it. She and Bill become lovers. Bill's old acquaintances Malcolm, Diane and Liam, vampires with no interest at all in mainstreaming, turn up at Sookie's door to look her over and enjoy frightening her, and their contempt for the rules makes plain how thin Bill's respectability is. Sookie learns that her great-uncle Bartlett, who molested her as a child and whom she had told Bill about, has been found dead; she does not have to ask who arranged it, and the knowledge sits badly with her. The tension between Bon Temps and the vampires breaks when locals burn the Monroe house where Malcolm, Diane and Liam sleep, killing all three, along with humans who were inside. The killings of local women have not stopped, and Sookie is increasingly certain she is on the list.

Eric summons Bill and Sookie to Fangtasia and makes his first real demand: Sookie is to read the minds of the bar's employees to find out who has been stealing from him. She identifies Long Shadow, the bartender, who lunges at her across the bar and is staked by Eric on the spot, drenching Sookie in blood. Bill is then called away to New Orleans on vampire business and leaves Bubba, an unstable vampire made from a famous singer, to guard the house while he is gone. In Bon Temps another young woman connected with Jason is strangled, and this time the evidence is enough for the police to arrest him. Sookie, frightened, grieving, and now certain that she is what the murderer actually wants, is left with a guard she cannot rely on and no idea which familiar face is doing the killing.

Sitting with Arlene and her children, Sookie catches an image out of a mind that tells her who the killer is: Rene Lenier, Arlene's former husband and Jason's workmate on the road crew. Years earlier his own sister took a vampire lover, and Rene strangled her for it; since then he has been killing women in the parish who did the same, which is why Maudette Pickens and Dawn Green died, and why Adele Stackhouse died in her granddaughter's place. Rene attacks Sookie and very nearly kills her. She survives, badly hurt, he is stopped, and vampire blood pulls her back from the worst of the damage. In the middle of it she discovers that Sam Merlotte is a shapeshifter, and that the stray collie sleeping at her house had been her boss standing guard. Jason is released and cleared. Bill comes back from New Orleans holding a formal position among the vampires of the area, one that will keep taking him away from her. Sookie ends the book alive, publicly attached to a vampire, and known to Eric Northman as something worth owning.

characters.description: A witch and runner for Cincinnati's Inderland Security service. Rachel is talented, impulsive, and frustrated by a run of humiliating assignments. She wants work that matters and is prepared to leave the security of government employment to get it, despite the agency's severe rule against breaking a contract.
characters.name: Rachel Morgan

characters.description: A living vampire and highly regarded Inderland Security runner who works beside Rachel. Ivy is controlled, observant, and intimidating, with formidable combat skills and powerful connections in Cincinnati's vampire society. Her decision to follow Rachel out of the agency makes their departure far more consequential.
characters.name: Ivy Tamwood

characters.description: A pixy who scouts and provides aerial support on Rachel's assignments. Jenks is tiny, sharp-tongued, practical, and fiercely protective of his wife and many children. His knowledge of gardens, wards, and surveillance makes him an essential partner rather than a mascot.
characters.name: Jenks

characters.description: Rachel's supervisor at Inderland Security. Denon has been feeding her poor assignments and treats her resignation as a personal challenge to agency authority.
characters.name: Denon

characters.description: A rival Inderland Security runner who enjoys Rachel's professional troubles and is willing to profit from the contract placed on her after she quits.
characters.name: Francis Percy

characters.description: An elderly witch who lives near the partners' new church office. Keasley is a skilled healer and a steady source of practical advice when Rachel's choices leave her injured or magically compromised.
characters.name: Keasley

characters.description: A wealthy Cincinnati businessman whose polished civic image conceals a private organization with extensive magical and criminal reach. Rachel selects him as the target whose exposure might buy her freedom from Inderland Security's death contract.
characters.name: Trent Kalamack

characters.description: A young employee of Trent Kalamack who hires Rachel to locate a missing coworker. Her concern gives Rachel a legitimate route into the affairs of a man she already suspects of larger crimes.
characters.name: Sara Jane Gradenko

characters.description: The human captain of Cincinnati's Federal Inderland Bureau. Edden is wary of supernatural investigators but recognizes Rachel's usefulness and offers a possible official ally outside Inderland Security.
characters.name: Edden

characters.description: A human researcher Rachel meets while pursuing information that ordinary Inderlanders cannot easily obtain. Nick is knowledgeable about old texts and magic, curious about Rachel's world, and increasingly drawn into both her investigation and her personal life.
characters.name: Nick Sparagmos

characters.description: Trent Kalamack's chief security officer and closest aide. Jonathan is disciplined, suspicious of Rachel, and ready to use force to protect his employer and the secrets of the Kalamack estate.
characters.name: Jonathan Davaros

characters.description: A demon whose services can be reached through dangerous summoning magic. Algaliarept bargains precisely, exploits desperation, and treats every apparent favor as an opportunity to acquire leverage over the summoner.
characters.name: Algaliarept

recaps.ending: Rachel escapes Trent Kalamack's estate after surviving captivity and the lethal contest arranged for her while she is trapped in animal form. She learns that Trent and Jonathan are elves, a people widely believed to be gone, and that Trent's illicit work is tied to the survival of his species as well as to his criminal business. The discovery gives her knowledge that can hurt him but also makes her valuable enough that he does not simply dispose of her. Her attempt to expose him does not bring down his organization, leaving him as a powerful and ambiguous enemy. Rachel also survives Inderland Security's efforts to enforce its death contract and establishes Vampiric Charms in the church with Ivy and Jenks. Nick has become both an ally and a romantic interest, while Rachel's contact with Algaliarept leaves demon magic as a new source of danger. She ends the book independent and alive, but with Trent, the agency, vampire politics, and a demon all aware of her.
recaps.in_short: Witch and Inderland Security runner Rachel Morgan quits after months of bad assignments. Living vampire Ivy Tamwood and pixy Jenks leave with her, and the agency answers with a death contract. The three establish an independent service in an abandoned church. Seeking leverage that could keep her alive, Rachel investigates wealthy businessman Trent Kalamack for illegal biodrug activity while also tracing a missing employee. Human researcher Nick Sparagmos helps her navigate unfamiliar magic, and repeated attacks show how exposed she is outside the agency. Rachel infiltrates Trent's estate using a transformation charm but is captured and forced into a deadly animal contest. She escapes and discovers that Trent and his aide Jonathan are secretly elves and that his genetic work serves motives more complicated than profit. She cannot destroy Trent's organization, but she survives both him and the immediate contract threat. Vampiric Charms remains open, with Rachel, Ivy, and Jenks committed to their risky new partnership and demon Algaliarept now connected to Rachel's expanding magical troubles.

recaps.text: Rachel Morgan is a witch employed as a runner by Inderland Security, the supernatural law-enforcement agency in a Cincinnati transformed by the Turn. Frustrated by poor assignments and hostile supervision, she quits after a routine job. Her partner Jenks, a pixy, chooses to leave with her. More unexpectedly, Ivy Tamwood, one of the agency's best runners and a well-connected living vampire, also resigns. Their departure triggers the agency's death-contract policy, placing Rachel in immediate danger. The three take over an old church and begin planning an independent investigation service. Rachel understands that ordinary caution will not be enough: she needs a major success or leverage against a powerful target if she is to persuade the agency that killing her is more trouble than it is worth.

Rachel, Ivy, and Jenks establish their uneasy household and business in the church while assassins and rival runners test Rachel's defenses. Ivy's vampire instincts make sharing space complicated, but her resources and reputation are also a major protection. Rachel chooses wealthy civic figure Trent Kalamack as the target of an investigation, suspecting that his legitimate businesses conceal illegal biodrug trafficking. Sara Jane Gradenko, a Kalamack employee worried about a missing coworker, gives Rachel a case that overlaps with those suspicions. Human FIB captain Edden offers a wary line to official cooperation, and Nick Sparagmos helps Rachel research magic and information that supernatural institutions keep guarded. Rachel's search begins to connect the missing person, Trent's organization, and substances whose distribution could expose him.

Rachel presses her investigation despite attacks, magical mishaps, and the growing strain of living with Ivy. She and Nick become closer as he helps her prepare charms and interpret material outside her training. Jenks scouts Trent's grounds and tracks details that full-sized investigators would miss. Trent remains publicly composed and difficult to touch; his security chief Jonathan treats Rachel as a direct threat. The more Rachel learns, the clearer it becomes that Trent's private laboratories and criminal contacts are real, but obtaining evidence that will survive official scrutiny is harder than identifying the pattern. Rachel decides that observation from outside the estate is insufficient and prepares to enter in a form that can pass through its defenses.

Using a difficult transformation charm, Rachel takes animal form and infiltrates Trent Kalamack's estate. The plan gives her access that a direct approach never could, but it also leaves her unable to defend herself in familiar ways. She finds further signs that Trent's operations involve both illicit drugs and closely guarded biological work. Trent and Jonathan detect the intrusion and capture her before she can leave cleanly. Rachel's investigation shifts into survival: she must conceal what she knows, understand why Trent is interested in her, and escape while trapped in a body his people can confine. Her earlier certainty that he is merely a polished drug lord begins to look incomplete, although the nature of the larger secret is not yet safe or clear.

Still held on Trent's property, Rachel is placed in a lethal contest against other transformed captives. She relies on her instincts, the limited magic available to her, and help from allies trying to reach her. The ordeal confirms Trent's ruthlessness and shows that Jonathan will protect his employer without hesitation. It also exposes contradictions in Trent's conduct: he wants Rachel contained, but his interest in her history and abilities keeps him from treating her as disposable. With escape routes closing, demon magic enters the struggle, adding a danger whose bargains can outlast the immediate crisis. Rachel survives the contest, but the decisive truths about Trent and the outcome of her conflict with him remain concealed until she gets free.

Rachel escapes Trent's estate alive and learns the secret behind some of its extraordinary security and research: Trent and Jonathan are elves, members of a people believed to have disappeared, and Trent's genetic work is connected to preserving that hidden population. His criminal activity remains real, but the discovery makes his aims more complicated than Rachel assumed and gives each of them dangerous knowledge about the other. Rachel cannot produce a clean public victory that destroys his organization, so Trent remains powerful and their rivalry continues. She nevertheless survives Inderland Security's immediate attempts to collect its death contract and proves that her new firm cannot be removed easily. Rachel, Ivy, and Jenks keep the church as the home of Vampiric Charms. Nick is now personally involved with Rachel, while her encounter with Algaliarept leaves her aware that demon bargains may become another lasting threat.

characters.description: A telepathic waitress in Bon Temps, married to Eric Northman by vampire custom and quietly carrying a cluviel dor, a fairy token good for a single wish, which she has told almost no one about. Her marriage is failing under the weight of a contract she was never meant to see, promising Eric to another vampire monarch, and her patience with the whole supernatural world is close to gone.
characters.name: Sookie Stackhouse

characters.description: The Viking vampire sheriff of Area Five, holding Louisiana territory with the king's regent conveniently dead and the king himself paying close attention. He is under an obligation his dead maker made for him and has not found a way to talk to Sookie about it, which is doing more damage than the obligation itself.
characters.name: Eric Northman

characters.description: Eric's child and second, sharper-tongued than ever since losing her lover Miriam. She is impatient with her maker's paralysis over the Oklahoma contract and blunt with Sookie about what it will cost both of them.
characters.name: Pam Ravenscroft

characters.description: The shapeshifter who owns Merlotte's and Sookie's employer and oldest friend in town. He has taken her on as a business partner in the bar, and his relationship with the werewolf enforcer Jannalynn Hopper is one of the few things he and Sookie do not discuss honestly.
characters.name: Sam Merlotte

characters.description: Sookie's vampire neighbor, fully recovered and serving Eric loyally. He has stopped asking Sookie for anything and become simply dependable, which she finds harder to argue with than his old persistence.
characters.name: Bill Compton

characters.description: Sookie's part-fairy cousin, who runs the club Hooligans in Monroe as a haven for the fae stranded in this world. He has been away a great deal, is evasive about where, and has developed a marked interest in what Sookie keeps in her house.
characters.name: Claude Crane

characters.description: Sookie's great-uncle, restored to himself since the curse on him was broken and living in her attic. He is warm, capable and openly homesick for a world whose doors were shut behind him.
characters.name: Dermot Brigant

characters.description: The vampire king of Nevada, Louisiana and Arkansas, visiting Shreveport with his retinue. He is charming, meticulous, and openly curious about what became of the regent he left in charge of the state.
characters.name: Felipe de Castro

characters.description: A young woman with were and fairy blood who turns up at a party at Eric's house offering herself as a blood donor, and makes a point of doing it in front of Sookie. She is nervous underneath the performance and appears to be following someone else's instructions.
characters.name: Kym Rowe

characters.description: The Long Tooth pack's enforcer and Sam's girlfriend, small, sharp and violent, who has never accepted Sookie's place in Sam's life or in the pack's affairs.
characters.name: Jannalynn Hopper

characters.description: Eric's day man, a werewolf who values his privacy and does his job precisely. He is drawn into the investigation because Eric needs someone who can move around in daylight and be trusted.
characters.name: Mustapha Khan

characters.description: An elf living at Hooligans among Claude's collection of stranded fae, cheerful, hungry and entirely unbothered by human squeamishness. He is friendly to Sookie in a way that does not reassure her.
characters.name: Bellenos

characters.description: A wealthy New Orleans developer and the father of Sookie's friend Amelia. He has known since the storm that Sookie's family possessed a fairy object of real power, and he wants it.
characters.name: Copley Carmichael

characters.description: Debbie Pelt's younger sister, who has spent years blaming Sookie for Debbie's disappearance and has been jailed and warned off more than once without effect. She is out again and has stopped pretending to want anything but Sookie dead.
characters.name: Sandra Pelt

characters.description: Sookie's great-grandfather and prince of the fairies, who shut Faery behind him and has been beyond reach ever since. Matters on the human side have grown serious enough to bring him back.
characters.name: Niall Brigant

recaps.ending: Jannalynn Hopper is exposed as the person who arranged for Kym Rowe to be sent to Eric's party, a scheme meant to discredit Eric in front of the visiting king and clear Sookie out of Sam's life; Kym's death was part of the machinery. Jannalynn does not survive the confrontation that follows, and neither, briefly, does Sam: he is killed in the fighting, and Sookie uses her one wish, the cluviel dor, to bring him back to life. It works, and it costs her everything the token might have been saved for. Eric, whose freedom from the Oklahoma marriage contract was the obvious use for a single wish, understands exactly what she chose and cannot forgive it; their marriage is effectively over from that moment even though neither of them says so outright. Niall Brigant returns from Faery and reveals that Claude has been working against Sookie and after the cluviel dor himself; he takes Claude back through the door for judgment, and Dermot chooses to go home with him, leaving Sookie's house empty of fairies. Felipe de Castro leaves Louisiana without proving anything about Victor Madden's disappearance but without being satisfied either. Sam is alive, changed by having died, and does not yet know what Sookie spent to bring him back.
recaps.in_short: Felipe de Castro comes to Shreveport with his retinue, still curious about the regent who vanished, and at a party at Eric's house a young half-fairy named Kym Rowe offers Eric her blood in front of Sookie. Hours later Kym is found dead in Eric's yard, and Eric is the obvious suspect in front of the one vampire he cannot afford to look guilty to. Sookie investigates while her marriage collapses under the contract pledging Eric to the vampire queen of Oklahoma, while her fairy cousin Claude behaves more and more strangely, and while Sandra Pelt makes one final attempt on her life. The trail behind Kym leads to Jannalynn Hopper, the werewolf enforcer dating Sam, who arranged the whole display to ruin Eric. The confrontation that ends it kills Sam, and Sookie spends her one fairy wish on bringing him back rather than on freeing Eric from Oklahoma. Niall returns to take Claude away for treachery, Dermot goes home to Faery with him, and Sookie and Eric are finished.

recaps.text: Sookie Stackhouse is a telepathic waitress in Bon Temps, Louisiana, where vampires and shapeshifters both live openly. She is married by vampire custom to Eric Northman, sheriff of Area Five, whose territory belongs to Felipe de Castro, king of Nevada; Eric, Pam, Sookie and several allies recently killed the king's regent Victor Madden in secret, and nobody knows whether that will stay hidden. Sookie is part fairy through her great-grandfather Prince Niall Brigant, who ended a fairy war fought over his human-blooded descendants and then closed Faery permanently, stranding her cousin Claude and her great-uncle Dermot on this side; both live in her house. Sorting her grandmother's things, Sookie learned that her real grandfather was the fairy Fintan and found the gift he left behind: a cluviel dor, which grants its holder a single wish. She also found papers showing that Eric's dead maker promised him in marriage to Freyda, the vampire queen of Oklahoma, an obligation Eric knew about and hid from her.

Felipe de Castro arrives in Shreveport with his companions for a stay of several days, ostensibly social, in fact an inquiry into what became of Victor Madden. Eric has to entertain him, which means a party at his house with Sookie present and every vampire in the area on display. Sookie and Eric are barely speaking about the Oklahoma contract and are pretending otherwise in public. During the party a young woman named Kym Rowe, carrying were and fairy blood, walks in and offers Eric her throat in front of everyone, and he takes it. Sookie leaves in a fury. Later that night Kym Rowe is found dead in Eric's yard, strangled, with the king of Louisiana on the premises and Eric the last person known to have fed from her.

The death has to be solved quickly, because Felipe cannot ignore a human murdered on his sheriff's property and Eric cannot afford any scrutiny at all with Victor Madden's disappearance still unexplained. Sookie starts working out who Kym Rowe was and who sent her: the girl's approach was staged, her blood was chosen to be irresistible, and someone paid for the performance. The investigation takes Sookie to Hooligans, Claude's club in Monroe, now a colony of stranded fae including the elf Bellenos, where she is welcomed with an enthusiasm that unsettles her. Claude himself has been absent a great deal and answers questions about it badly.

The trail behind Kym Rowe leads into werewolf circles and toward the Long Tooth pack's enforcer, Jannalynn Hopper, whose motive for humiliating Eric is not obvious and whose relationship with Sam is looking more calculated the closer Sookie looks at it. At the same time Sookie learns she is being watched by people acting for Copley Carmichael, Amelia's father, who has worked out that her family owns a fairy object of real power and intends to have it. The cluviel dor becomes a liability rather than a comfort. Eric, cornered between the king's suspicion and the Oklahoma contract, withdraws further, and Sookie realizes he has been treating the marriage as already lost.

Sandra Pelt, out of custody and past all restraint, makes her final attempt on Sookie's life, and Sookie kills her; the body is disposed of quietly, ending a feud that has followed her for years. The pressure around the cluviel dor keeps rising, with Copley Carmichael's people, the fae at Hooligans and Sookie's own household all circling it, and Sookie increasingly certain that Claude is not simply curious. The Kym Rowe investigation closes on Jannalynn, and Sookie has to decide how to tell Sam that the woman he is with arranged a killing to serve pack politics.

Jannalynn is exposed: she arranged for Kym Rowe to be sent to Eric's party to disgrace him in front of the king and to break up his marriage, and Kym's death followed from it. The confrontation turns into a fight, Jannalynn does not survive it, and neither does Sam, who is killed in front of Sookie. Sookie uses the cluviel dor on him, spending her single wish to bring him back to life, and it works. Eric knows immediately what she could have used it for instead, and their marriage does not survive the knowledge, even though the Oklahoma contract still stands over him. Niall Brigant comes back through the closed door, reveals that Claude has been working against Sookie and after the cluviel dor for himself, and takes him away to be judged; Dermot chooses to go home to Faery with them. Felipe de Castro leaves Louisiana with his questions about Victor Madden unanswered. Sookie is left with Merlotte's, a resurrected friend who does not know what his life cost, and no husband.

characters.description: A former political prisoner living with the lasting effects of abduction, rape, and torture under her country's recently ended dictatorship. She is married to Gerardo and distrusts the fragile new democracy's willingness to confront crimes committed against survivors like her.
characters.name: Paulina Salas

characters.description: Paulina's husband, a lawyer asked to serve on a presidential commission investigating human-rights abuses that ended in death. He supports the democratic transition and believes in legal procedure, but the commission's narrow mandate strains his relationship with Paulina, whose abuse it cannot examine.
characters.name: Gerardo Escobar

characters.description: A physician who helps Gerardo after his car suffers a flat tire and later visits the couple's isolated house. Polite, educated, and apparently sympathetic to the new political order, he becomes the focus of Paulina's alarm when she hears his voice.
characters.name: Roberto Miranda

recaps.ending: Gerardo persuades Roberto to produce the confession Paulina demands, privately supplying details from her imprisonment so Roberto can construct an account. Paulina has deliberately altered some details when speaking to Gerardo, however, and Roberto's corrections align with what she remembers, reinforcing her certainty that he was the doctor who abused her. With the deadline she set approaching, Paulina confronts Roberto with this test and insists that only genuine remorse, not performance, can save him. The immediate confrontation ends without providing a simple public verdict. Later, Paulina and Gerardo attend a concert where Schubert's quartet is being performed. The truth commission has completed work within its restricted mandate, leaving many crimes such as Paulina's outside its official account. Paulina sees Roberto in the audience, or imagines seeing him, and the three remain connected by an unresolved past that neither private vengeance nor the new state's limited justice has conclusively settled.
recaps.in_short: In a country newly returned to democracy, lawyer Gerardo Escobar joins a commission limited to investigating abuses that resulted in death. His wife Paulina, a survivor of torture and rape whom the commission cannot help, hears the voice of visiting doctor Roberto Miranda and identifies him as the physician who supervised and joined in her abuse while playing Schubert. She takes Roberto captive, conducts a private trial, and demands a full confession. Roberto denies knowing her, while Gerardo tries to prevent violence and secure his release. Gerardo gives Roberto details of Paulina's ordeal so he can make a convincing statement, but Paulina has planted false details; Roberto corrects them in ways that confirm her suspicions. The confrontation produces no clean legal resolution. In an epilogue at a concert, after the truth commission has reported within its narrow limits, Paulina sees or imagines Roberto across the hall as the music associated with her torture plays, leaving guilt, punishment, and recovery unresolved.

recaps.text: In an unnamed country emerging from dictatorship, Gerardo Escobar returns to his isolated coastal home after a flat tire. He tells his wife Paulina that the president has asked him to join a truth commission, but its mandate covers only abuses that led to death. Paulina, who was abducted, tortured, and raped by agents of the former regime, resents a process that excludes surviving victims and doubts the new authorities' courage. A stranger named Roberto Miranda arrives, having helped Gerardo on the road, and stays to talk about the political transition. Listening from another room, Paulina becomes convinced that his voice belongs to the doctor who participated in her torture years earlier, when she was blindfolded and unable to see him.

While the men sleep, Paulina takes Gerardo's gun, binds Roberto to a chair, and reveals her accusation. She also finds a recording of Schubert's string quartet known as Death and the Maiden in Roberto's car, matching the music played during her captivity. Roberto insists that he is innocent and that the recording is common; Gerardo is horrified by Paulina's improvised tribunal and argues that recognition by voice and manner is not proof. Paulina demands that Roberto confess fully, saying that she needs his acknowledgment more than formal punishment. She forces Gerardo into the role of defense counsel but controls the room and the weapon. The dispute sets her remembered certainty against the safeguards Gerardo believes the new democracy must observe.

Gerardo speaks privately with Paulina about her imprisonment, learning details she had never fully shared with him, and tries to negotiate a way for Roberto to survive. Roberto continues to deny being her torturer but agrees to record a confession if it will secure his release. Gerardo supplies him with information from Paulina's account so that the statement will satisfy her. The resulting confession describes the doctor's movement from detached medical supervision into active cruelty and sexual violence. Paulina listens carefully rather than simply accepting it. She has not treated the confession as an empty ritual: she is testing whether Roberto possesses knowledge that Gerardo could not have given him.

Paulina reveals that she intentionally gave Gerardo inaccurate details. Roberto corrected those details in his confession, strengthening her belief that he can only know them because he was present during her torture. Roberto still frames his statement as something composed under threat, while Paulina demands genuine recognition of what was done to her. The private trial reaches its deadline without yielding a conventional verdict or a stable division between proof, confession, and coercion. Later, Gerardo and Paulina attend a concert after the truth commission has completed its restricted work. Schubert's Death and the Maiden is performed, and Paulina sees, or may imagine she sees, Roberto in the audience. The image leaves the three figures facing one another across a society that has moved toward democracy without fully accounting for the violence carried into its present.

characters.description: Sixteen, and carrying more than she admits to anyone. She is one of the most capable young sorcerers in the country, fluent with air and fire and dangerous with shadows, and she is still the Necromancers' favourite candidate for a prophecy she wants nothing to do with. Since the Remnant outbreak she has been sleeping badly, lying more often, and letting her mirror duplicate live an increasing share of her ordinary life. Her mother is expecting a baby, her boyfriend knows almost nothing about what she does, and her true name has been sealed away where she hopes it will stay.
characters.name: Valkyrie Cain

characters.description: The skeleton detective: Elemental, insufferable, and the best investigator the Irish Sanctuary has, whether or not it wants him. He has been Valkyrie's partner for four years and has never told her the whole of what he did in the war against Mevolent, and he deflects every attempt to ask.
characters.name: Skulduggery Pleasant

characters.description: The Teleporter, and Valkyrie's boyfriend, who can step anywhere he can picture and cannot follow her into most of her life. He is loyal, funny, and increasingly aware that he is being managed.
characters.name: Fletcher Renn

characters.description: The scarred tailor who can turn his skin to stone, now an Elder of the Irish Sanctuary and a reluctant politician. He is one of the few people who will tell both Skulduggery and Valkyrie the truth about themselves.
characters.name: Ghastly Bespoke

characters.description: The Grand Mage of the Irish Sanctuary, one of the Dead Men and an old comrade of Skulduggery's from the war, holding a difficult office with charm and a good deal of quiet calculation.
characters.name: Erskine Ravel

characters.description: The veiled Elder of the Sanctuary, who speaks for the Children of the Spider and treats every question as an intrusion.
characters.name: Madame Mist

characters.description: The keeper of Dublin's great private library, still trading information and still declining to talk about her own past with the people who worship the Faceless Ones. That past has become harder to leave alone.
characters.name: China Sorrows

characters.description: Valkyrie's closest friend, taken by a Remnant at the end of the last case and now walking around wearing her own face with none of her own loyalties. She is as good with a sword as she ever was, in an excellent mood about it, and entirely on the other side.
characters.name: Tanith Low

characters.description: The Texan killer with hollows where his eyes should be, who travels through solid ground and works for whoever is paying. He has been keeping unusual company lately.
characters.name: Billy-Ray Sanguine

characters.description: The Necromancer who taught Valkyrie the magic of shadow and death. He has spent years believing she is the Death Bringer his order has been waiting for, and he is running out of time to be proved right within his own Temple.
characters.name: Solomon Wreath

characters.description: A young Necromancer of the Irish Temple, sullen, resentful and dismissive of the attention that has always gone to the outsider Valkyrie Cain instead of to her. She is more ambitious than her rank allows and has attracted the interest of people willing to use that.
characters.name: Melancholia St Clair

characters.description: A cleric of the Necromancer Temple: fussy, obsequious and much cleverer than he lets people see. He has his own reading of the Death Bringer prophecy and his own plans for who should fulfil it.
characters.name: Vandameer Craven

characters.description: The High Priest of the Irish Necromancer Temple, an old man presiding over an order that has waited generations for its prophecy and is losing patience with waiting.
characters.name: Auron Tenebrae

characters.description: The vampire who has kept himself apart from the packs and close to Valkyrie. His interest in her has not faded, his self-control is less reliable than he claims, and what began as protectiveness has stopped looking like it.
characters.name: Caelan

characters.description: A striking, ambitious sorcerer working to rebuild the Church of the Faceless as a respectable institution, with money, patience and a long memory. She and China Sorrows knew each other a very long time ago and neither of them enjoys being reminded of it.
characters.name: Eliza Scorn

characters.description: The Necromancer general who fought for Mevolent in black armour, vanished before the war ended and began killing again a year ago. Nobody has ever seen what is inside the armour, and everyone who has tried to corner him has failed.
characters.name: Lord Vile

characters.description: Valkyrie's baby sister, born to Desmond and Melissa Edgley: an entirely ordinary infant in a family with one member who is not, and a new reason for Valkyrie to keep her two lives from ever meeting.
characters.name: Alice Edgley

recaps.ending: The Passage is stopped. Melancholia St Clair, made into the Death Bringer by Vandameer Craven's ritual, is beaten and taken into custody with her power broken, and Craven does not survive the collapse of his own plan. Stopping her costs Skulduggery the thing he had spent centuries burying: he puts the armour on and becomes Lord Vile again, and Valkyrie is the one who has to bring him back out of it afterwards. The secret is now hers as well, and their partnership continues on the far side of it, changed and honest for the first time. Solomon Wreath's order is left discredited, its prophecy spent, and Wreath and Valkyrie part badly. Valkyrie ends the book with a newborn sister, Alice, a broken relationship with Fletcher after he learns about Caelan, and Caelan himself dead after his obsession turned into an attempt on her life. Eliza Scorn takes her revenge on China Sorrows by burning her library to the ground, destroying the collection China built her whole life around and leaving her with nothing but her reputation. Tanith Low is still possessed and still at large, still waiting for Darquesse, and Valkyrie's sealed true name is the one thing nobody has managed to touch.
recaps.in_short: The Necromancers have waited generations for the Death Bringer, the one who will end the division between the living and the dead, and Solomon Wreath has long believed it is Valkyrie. When she refuses, the cleric Vandameer Craven turns the resentful young Necromancer Melancholia St Clair into the Death Bringer instead, and the truth of what the prophecy requires comes out: the Passage would kill a great many people to buy immortality for whoever survives it. While Skulduggery and Valkyrie work to stop the Temple, Lord Vile returns in force, and Valkyrie learns who he is. After Serpine murdered Skulduggery's wife and child, Skulduggery came back from death consumed by rage, took up Necromancy and served Mevolent as Lord Vile, killing on an enormous scale while leading the Dead Men, and none of his friends ever knew. Skulduggery has to become Vile again to beat Melancholia, and Valkyrie has to pull him back. The Passage is prevented, Craven dies, Melancholia is broken, Caelan is killed, Valkyrie and Fletcher break up, her sister Alice is born, and Eliza Scorn burns China Sorrows's library.

recaps.text: Previously: Stephanie Edgley became Valkyrie Cain, partner to the skeleton detective Skulduggery Pleasant. She killed Nefarian Serpine with the Sceptre of the Ancients, stopped Baron Vengeous waking the Grotesquery, and learned she is descended from the last of the Ancients. When the Diablerie opened a portal at Aranmore Farm the Sanctuary's Elders and Mr Bliss were killed, and Skulduggery drove the Faceless One back through and was trapped in the dark gods' world until Valkyrie, the Teleporter Fletcher Renn and the Dead Men brought him home; Erskine Ravel became Grand Mage with Ghastly Bespoke and Madame Mist. In the last case, thousands of Remnants escaped and possessed their way through Ireland, Kenspeckle Grouse was killed, and Valkyrie discovered that her true name is Darquesse and that the sorcerer every Sensitive has seen destroying the world is her. She became Darquesse once, fought the returned Lord Vile to a standstill, and afterwards had her true name sealed. As the outbreak ended, a Remnant took Tanith Low, and the possessed Tanith escaped. Valkyrie has trained in Necromancy under Solomon Wreath, whose order awaits a figure called the Death Bringer.

Life is quieter than it has been and Valkyrie is worse for it. She is sixteen, sleeping badly, keeping her boyfriend Fletcher at arm's length from most of her existence and letting her mirror duplicate take over more and more of her ordinary life in Haggard, where her mother is expecting a baby. She is also still keeping company with Caelan, the vampire who has attached himself to her, which she has told nobody about. Skulduggery is working cases with her as usual, the Sanctuary under Erskine Ravel is stable, and the only real pressure is coming from the Necromancers, who want an answer from Valkyrie that she has no intention of giving.

The Necromancers, who draw their magic from death and shadow, have spent generations waiting for the Death Bringer: the sorcerer who will bring about the Passage and end the division between the living and the dead. Solomon Wreath has believed for years that Valkyrie is that person, which is why he taught her, and her refusal leaves his order without the future it has been promising itself. Bodies begin turning up in a pattern that points at the Temple, the possessed Tanith Low resurfaces, and Billy-Ray Sanguine is working for someone with money and a plan. Skulduggery and Valkyrie start pulling at the Necromancers, and the Temple closes ranks.

Inside the Temple, the cleric Vandameer Craven has been advancing a candidate of his own: Melancholia St Clair, a young Necromancer who has resented Valkyrie's place in the prophecy for years and who is willing to be made into something else. The High Priest Auron Tenebrae presides over an order that no longer agrees with itself. The ritual Craven puts Melancholia through is savage, and it works: she comes out of it far more powerful than any Necromancer should be, and she is not stable. What nobody outside the Temple has been told is what the Passage will actually cost.

The truth about the Passage comes out. Ending death for everyone who survives it requires an enormous amount of death first, and the Necromancers' promised gift to the world begins with killing on a scale that would be remembered for centuries. The Sanctuary moves against the Temple, and the Temple, with a Death Bringer of its own, is no longer inclined to be governed. At the same time Lord Vile returns in force. He kills without being challenged, ignores every attempt to negotiate, and is more than a match for anything the Sanctuary can field. Valkyrie's private life comes apart in parallel: Fletcher learns about Caelan, and Caelan's attentiveness curdles into something she cannot talk her way out of.

Valkyrie learns who Lord Vile is, and it is Skulduggery. When Serpine murdered his wife and child and tortured him to death, Skulduggery came back consumed by a rage that had nowhere to go, took up Necromancy, put on the black armour and served Mevolent as one of his generals, killing on a scale no one has ever fully counted. He did it while leading the Dead Men, and none of them knew; when he finally put Vile aside, he buried the whole of it and has never spoken of it since. The armour has come back because the thing that made it has never left him. Valkyrie has to decide what her partner is, and Skulduggery has to decide whether he can be trusted to keep the armour off.

Melancholia, fully in her power, moves to bring about the Passage, and nothing the Sanctuary has is enough to slow her down. Craven's control over his own creation proves to be a fiction. Valkyrie's baby sister Alice is born in the middle of it, an entirely ordinary thing in a life that has stopped containing any, and Valkyrie's determination to keep her family out of this hardens into the only rule she has left. She and Fletcher end their relationship, and Caelan, whose obsession has stopped resembling affection, becomes a danger she has to deal with herself. To stop Melancholia at all, Skulduggery will have to be Lord Vile again, with no guarantee that there will be anything left of Skulduggery afterwards.

Skulduggery puts the armour on, becomes Lord Vile and beats Melancholia, and Valkyrie is the one who brings him back out of it afterwards, which is the hardest thing either of them has done. The Passage is prevented, Melancholia is left broken and in custody, and Craven does not survive his own plan. The Necromancer Temple is discredited, its prophecy spent, and Valkyrie and Solomon Wreath part on terms that will not be repaired. Caelan is killed after turning on her, and she and Fletcher are finished. Her sister Alice is born safely into a family that still knows nothing. Eliza Scorn settles her account with China Sorrows by burning her library to the ground, destroying a lifetime's collection. Skulduggery's secret is now Valkyrie's too, and their partnership survives it, more honest than it has ever been. Tanith Low is still possessed and still at large, still certain that Darquesse is coming, and Valkyrie's true name remains sealed.

characters.description: A celebrated German author in his early fifties whose reputation rests on disciplined, formally controlled work. Widowed and solitary, he has organized his life around artistic duty until a sudden impulse to travel unsettles his carefully maintained routine.
characters.name: Gustav von Aschenbach

characters.description: An unknown man whom Aschenbach sees near a cemetery in Munich. His foreign-looking appearance and confrontational gaze stir vivid thoughts of distant landscapes and awaken Aschenbach's long-suppressed desire to travel.
characters.name: The Stranger

characters.description: An elderly passenger on the steamer to Venice who uses cosmetics, dyed hair, fashionable clothes, and drunken high spirits to pass among a group of young men. His attempt to disguise age repels Aschenbach.
characters.name: The Elderly Dandy

characters.description: A silent, unlicensed gondolier who takes Aschenbach toward the Lido despite being ordered to stop at San Marco. His pale appearance, abrupt manner, and unexplained disappearance after the journey make the ride disturbing.
characters.name: The Gondolier

characters.description: A beautiful Polish boy of about fourteen staying with his family at Aschenbach's hotel on the Lido. Fair-haired, reserved, and watched over by his mother, he immediately appears to the writer as an image of exceptional classical beauty.
characters.name: Tadzio

characters.description: An elegant Polish woman vacationing at the Lido with Tadzio, his sisters, and their attendants. Dignified and protective, she supervises the children's ordered routine and treats her son with particular tenderness.
characters.name: Tadzio's Mother

characters.description: The leader of a band of street performers who entertains guests on the hotel terrace. Insolent and watchful beneath his comic manner, he carries the smell of disinfectant and evades Aschenbach's questions about sickness in Venice.
characters.name: The Street Singer

characters.description: An English employee at a Venice travel office who answers Aschenbach honestly when local officials and hotel staff will not. He explains the danger spreading through the city and urges his visitor to leave at once.
characters.name: The English Clerk

recaps.ending: As the epidemic worsens, Aschenbach learns the truth from an English travel clerk but chooses neither to leave Venice nor to warn Tadzio's family. His restraint collapses into covert pursuit. After a disturbing dream, he lets a barber dye his hair and apply cosmetics, reproducing the false youth that had disgusted him on the voyage. Sick and exhausted, he continues following the Polish family and eats overripe strawberries in the infected city. On the nearly deserted beach, he watches Tadzio lose a struggle with another boy and then walk alone into the shallow sea. When Tadzio turns and gestures toward the horizon, Aschenbach imagines that the boy is beckoning him onward. He slumps in his chair and dies. The family departs, and the public receives news of the famous writer's death without knowing the private obsession and disintegration that preceded it.
recaps.in_short: Gustav von Aschenbach, a famous writer whose life is governed by discipline, yields to a sudden desire for travel and goes to Venice. At a hotel on the Lido he sees Tadzio, a beautiful Polish adolescent, and begins treating the boy as an embodiment of ideal form. When oppressive weather prompts him to leave, misplaced luggage gives him an excuse to return. His aesthetic admiration becomes an acknowledged infatuation, and he secretly follows Tadzio and his family. Meanwhile cholera spreads through Venice while authorities conceal it to protect tourism. Aschenbach discovers the danger but stays silent rather than risk the family's departure. Abandoning the dignity on which his public identity rests, he dyes his hair, wears cosmetics, and wanders the infected city after the boy. Ill and exhausted, he watches Tadzio from a beach chair, imagines the boy pointing him toward the horizon, and dies.

recaps.text: Gustav von Aschenbach, a renowned Munich-based writer, leaves his work for an evening walk after finding himself unusually restless. Near a cemetery he notices a foreign-looking stranger whose appearance calls up an intense vision of tropical wilderness. The encounter awakens a desire to escape the controlled, laborious pattern of Aschenbach's life. He has rarely permitted himself leisure, but now decides that travel may provide the brief interruption his exhausted imagination needs. The impulse is less a settled plan than a rupture in a routine built on self-command.

Aschenbach resolves to travel after the stranger's appearance awakens a powerful restlessness. His public stature has been earned through an art of endurance: physically delicate from childhood, he trained himself to work with strict regularity and made dignity, restraint, and perseverance the foundations of his writing. His books have brought official honors and a noble title, while his private life has narrowed after the death of his wife and the marriage of his daughter. This history explains both the authority of his reputation and the strain beneath it. The journey he now contemplates represents a rare surrender to appetite and chance.

After an unsatisfying stop on the Adriatic, Aschenbach chooses Venice. During the voyage he is disgusted by an elderly man using clothes, dye, and cosmetics to imitate the young companions around him. An unauthorized gondolier then carries him toward his hotel against his instructions and disappears before he can be paid. At the Lido hotel, Aschenbach notices Tadzio, a Polish boy of extraordinary beauty travelling with his mother, sisters, and attendants. He studies the family from a distance and takes growing pleasure in seeing the boy at meals and on the beach. The humid air soon makes him feel unwell, so he decides to leave. At the station, however, his luggage is mistakenly sent on without him. Relieved by the excuse, he returns to the hotel and recognizes that the thought of losing sight of Tadzio had made departure painful.

Back at the Lido, Aschenbach arranges his days around observing Tadzio. The boy's appearance leads him into reflections on classical beauty, art, and the relation between physical form and spiritual aspiration. He begins following the Polish family through Venice while preserving the outward habits of a respectable hotel guest. His attention is no longer simply that of an artist studying an ideal model. Tadzio becomes aware of being watched and sometimes seems to respond. When the boy smiles at him, Aschenbach privately admits that he loves him, though no direct relationship exists between them. The discipline that shaped his life and career is giving way to a consuming attachment sustained by distance and fantasy.

Signs of disease appear across Venice: disinfectant odors fill the streets, notices warn against certain foods, and visitors quietly depart. Officials and hotel staff offer evasions, but an English travel clerk tells Aschenbach that cholera has spread from Asia and is being concealed to protect the tourist economy. He advises immediate departure. Aschenbach imagines warning Tadzio's mother, yet remains silent because the family's safety would mean losing the boy. His secret pursuit becomes more desperate. After a dream of a violent pagan rite overwhelms his remaining self-control, he submits to a barber who dyes his hair and covers his aging face with cosmetics. He follows the family through the unhealthy city and eats overripe strawberries. On the beach, a weakened Aschenbach watches Tadzio struggle with another boy, then walk into the shallow water and turn toward the horizon. Interpreting Tadzio's gesture as a summons, Aschenbach collapses in his chair and dies. News of the distinguished author's death reaches a public unaware of his final obsession.

characters.description: Chicago's professional wizard, still carrying the White Council's war with the Red Court on his shoulders. Hired to recover a stolen holy relic and simultaneously challenged to a formal duel that could end the war - with his own life as the stake - Harry spends the book squeezed between the vampires, a cabal of fallen angels, and the return of the woman he loves. His stubborn refusal to hand any fight to someone else, and his instinct to shield everyone near him, drive both his victories and his costliest choices.
characters.name: Harry Dresden

characters.description: A Red Court warlord, courtly and disciplined, who arrives in Chicago with a formal proposal: a duel to the death with Harry under the Accords, the supernatural world's code of law, to end the war between the Red Court and the White Council. Ortega presents himself as a soldier seeking to stop a ruinous conflict, and unlike most of his kind he keeps a veneer of honor - but he is a centuries-old predator, and the duel is not as clean an offer as it seems.
characters.name: Paolo Ortega

characters.description: Harry's former girlfriend, the reporter left half-turned by the Red Court, returned to Chicago after more than a year away. Susan has learned to control her thirst with the help of the Fellowship of St. Giles, an organization of the half-turned who fight the Red Court, and she has become faster, stronger, and far more dangerous. Her reunion with Harry is charged with everything unresolved between them - love, guilt, and the hard fact that a moment of lost control could destroy them both.
